install.effects: Frozen dependency installation with the pinned pnpm and lockfile.

setup.effects: Builds Lamp, migrates local data, saves private settings, claims the first owner through Base operator-auth and initializes product settings.

dev.effects: Serves Lamp locally with Base keyed owner dev identity and silently suppressed mail.

preview.effects: Serves the fixed production build locally. Sign in locally with rer dev.

build.effects: Builds the production Worker and assets with private local settings set aside.

verify.effects: Runs Lamp's complete local verification: source, Workers, browser and generated-artifact checks; no hosted acceptance claim.

reset.effects: After confirmation removes local data, owner, generated private settings and installer state; keeps source, exports and deployment receipts.

deploy.effects: Runs Lamp's Cloudflare pipeline: input validation, resource setup and migrations, build, secret upload, Worker deploy and health check. Full verification runs separately with rer verify. --dry-run builds and validates locally with no provider request.

export.effects: Export the local copy with --output, or run the declared hosted-export argv with --target remote. Hosted output keeps the seed's own format; the summary names its path and exit status.

import.effects: Restores a verified archive into an empty local installation after --yes. node scripts/setup.mjs --restore-from covers a deployed installation.

doctor.effects: Read-only tool, configuration and state diagnostics naming missing inputs.

describe.effects: Describes commands, flags, pins and local state without running project commands.

release.effects: Base release producer: receipts, validation and gates; never pushes or deploys.

demo.effects: A throwaway demo of this seed (rer dev --demo): fresh data in .rer/demo/START (deleted when it stops: --stop, Ctrl-C or its end, one hour by default or --idle-timeout), the saved owner signed in through the demo persona, a separate RER_OWNER_OPEN link for single-use native owner entry on loopback (15-minute expiry; never saved), the seed's demo data, Demo in the app name and title, real public reads/checks and simulated external writes (RER_DEMO=1; the checkout's own data is never touched).

adopt-edition.effects: Add edition.json and sources.lock.json for the existing tracked local source, preserving declared project identity and existing copy/composition records. Create an empty base-copies.json only when none exists. Review and stage the new authoring inputs; no source regeneration, install setup or commit.

refresh-base.effects: Consent to each declared edition edit with repeatable --edition-migration ID; refresh leaves the edit owed. Refresh recorded Base copies to --ref FULL_COMMIT, preserving acknowledged adaptations and applied migrations; announce removed singleton retirement. Deliver invoked workflow helpers atomically; adopt tracked known historical Verify templates and preserve divergent workflows with adoption notices. Acquire committed source from the declared Base repository (default https://github.com/runeditrun/base.git), or read immutable trees, blobs and ancestry through authenticated gh with --from-api, or use --base CHECKOUT or --base-archive DIRECTORY with --ref FULL_COMMIT for an exported source tree. --offline requires --base or --base-archive and never acquires remote source. Refuse incomplete Git checkouts without changing their records. Review the diff and run edition tests before committing.

signin.effects: A one-time sign-in link for the hosted owner, without mail. Uses the Cloudflare credentials that deployed --environment (default production; from the environment or --env-file) to write a single-use grant for the recorded owner into that deployment's auth database, then prints the link once to this terminal; it is never saved. The link works once, only for that owner, expires within 15 minutes, and its use is recorded in the owner's audit log. Signed in this way, the owner can correct a wrong email in settings.

value.value: # Move in from another status page

After building the candidate, `pnpm sorry:receipt --capture /unchanged/capture --key-file /private/test.pem --out /new/output` (reading the request metadata from `/unchanged/capture.metadata.json`) verifies a public capture in a disposable test installation and signs its receipt; reviewed receipts live in `docs/receipts/` and their public keys belong only in the consumer's test trust store.

1. Sign in and open **Settings → Move in** (`/app/move-in`). Choose the matching
   source in the **Source** menu; its source-specific instructions are below.
2. Enter the source page ID and API key or token where supported, or upload saved provider JSON.
   Credential reads use fixed provider origins and `GET` requests only. Keys are
   used for that read, are not stored, and are not forwarded through redirects.
   Sorry's authenticated export runs locally as described below; its key never
   enters Lamp's Worker.
3. Choose **Run dry run**. Nothing has been written. Review the read, imported,
   changed, skipped and refused counts and the reason for every non-imported row.
   You can download the exact responses read and use those saved files later.
4. Check the review box and choose **Import**. Large imports may pause in batches;
   choose **Continue** until the job is complete. This does not send mail.
5. Open **Settings → Cutover** (`/app/cutover`). Before import it shows proposed
   destinations; after import it shows surviving records. Review the first 25 old
   public addresses, the total address count, unavailable links, reader gaps and
   eligible invitation count.
6. Choose **Send invitations** in Cutover. This is the only move-in action that
   sends mail. It sends one invitation to each eligible pending email subscriber;
   repeat for any remaining batch before the confirmation deadline.
   For Sorry, complete the hostname switch and observation window first; its
   imported subscriber candidates are held until that readiness check, for at
   most 30 days.
7. Point a hostname you control to Lamp using [the custom-domain guide](domains.md),
   or keep the deployment's default public address. Select that public origin in
   Cutover. Selecting it records your choice; it does not check DNS.
8. After switching, use **Check opens** for the listed links. These checks run in
   your browser without cookies or credentials, follow redirects and confirm a
   successful HTML page at the exact Lamp destination. A network, CORS or browser
   access error does not prove that a link works or that it is broken.
9. Keep the old page available through the pending subscribers' confirmation
   deadlines. Update old links, feeds, widgets and API readers before retiring it.

Move in, `rer` and Business imports share one import door. **Run dry run**
uploads the saved responses, unchanged, as one JSON envelope (`source`, `files`
and the form's `pageId`, `publicAccessAcknowledged` and `publicUrl`) to the
door's owner surface, `/api/operator/import/*`, as the signed-in owner, and
shows the door's plan; a key or public page is first read into saved responses
(`POST /api/app/statuspage-import/fetch`, which writes nothing). **Import**
applies exactly the fingerprint you reviewed, in bounded steps. A later import
of the same source is that import's catch-up (see below), and selecting the same
files again reads as already imported. A new dry run replaces one you did not
import. Importing again a source whose import you undid uploads it afresh,
apart from records that undo kept because you changed them in Lamp (see
[Repeat, undo and full-install restore](#repeat-undo-and-full-install-restore)).
A dry run plans the page as it is at that moment and imports for 30 minutes;
after that **Import** answers "This dry run has expired. Run the dry run again."
and changes nothing. **Your imports** lists your imports ("approved by") and Business imports
("approved via Business by") together; undo the newest import of a source first.
Imports made before the door keep their own read, Continue and Undo.
## From setup, without a key

When setup finds the Statuspage, Instatus or Better Stack page your site links to
(or one at `status.<your domain>` that names your site), **Bring its incident history too** reads that
page's public feeds once more, keyless, and imports them through the same door:
Statuspage's `/api/v2/summary.json` and `/api/v2/incidents.json` (its 50 newest
incidents), Instatus's `/summary.json`, `/v2/components.json` and `/history.atom`,
and Better Stack's `/index.json` and `/feed`. The envelope's `files` are those
responses, and `components` lists the components you kept at setup, by the page's
own IDs, with your names. Only resolved incidents come, each update at its original
time; nothing still open on the page, no maintenance and no subscribers. Component
states come only where the feeds state them (Statuspage updates, and the reports a
Better Stack page still shows); any other incident is history that names the
components it lists, without changing their history. An incident about components
you left out stays out. **Your imports** lists the import, and Undo removes it.
A full Move in of the same page later, with its key or saved responses, is that
import's catch-up (see below): the history it brought is replaced in place unless
you changed it in Lamp, nothing it holds is imported again, and what setup did not
bring (maintenance, subscribers, the components you left out) is added without
notifying anyone.

Deleting a subscriber, and the expiry of an unconfirmed or held one, also erases
that address from import custody: its imported record becomes an erased entry,
and the door's retained uploads and plan snapshots, which hold whole exports, are
withdrawn. Earlier imports still undo. An export that still holds an erased
subscriber is refused (`source_erased`); remove that subscriber from it first.

Cutover lists the first 25 public addresses. A live check covers only the rows
shown there; it does not validate the rest of the total automatically. A hostname
switch affects the address you control. It does not transfer or control a
provider-owned shortlink host, so keep its redirect active or update links that
still use that host.

These are `.json` files containing the records your old provider returned when
its API was asked for components, incidents or subscribers. They are not
screenshots, CSV exports or a browser's saved public web page. Upload the files
unchanged and together; Lamp reads them without using an API key. Instatus also
needs the page ID so it can select the right page from those files.

If you have no such files, use the source account/API option in Move in, or ask
the person managing your old status page to capture them using the provider
instructions below. **Download these saved responses** after a dry run also gives you
files you can use for a later saved-response import. Keep them private: subscriber
files can contain personal information. Do not put them in Git.
Subject to the selected source's documented fields and the dry-run report:

| Source data | Lamp result |
| --- | --- |
| Component groups and components | Native groups and components; supported names, descriptions, ordering and relationships are retained. |
| Incidents and supplied updates | Native incident history at the source times the reader supports; notifications are not replayed. |
| Scheduled maintenance | Native maintenance windows and source-specific history where supported; a window already over is imported as completed. |
| Eligible email subscribers | Pending Lamp subscriptions; Sorry candidates are first held for cutover. Each person must confirm an invitation before the deadline. |

The sources do not expose identical fields. Each source section and the dry run
name omitted, changed, skipped or refused records; relevant source-specific
defaults are described below.

Dry runs, import, **Continue**, job reads, re-running an import, undo and Cutover
checks send no mail or trigger customer notices for imported history. Imported
history appears on the public page. Only **Send invitations** sends mail.
Eligible email rows stay pending until they confirm; Sorry candidates are held
until released to pending after cutover. Unconfirmed or unsubscribed source rows
are skipped where the source provides those states; the reader differences are
described below. Lamp permits at most one invitation per
imported subscriber and claims it before the mail transport call. A claimed or
uncertain send is not automatically retried. A transport acceptance does not
prove inbox delivery. Local development silently suppresses mail and retains no
invitations to open; use a hosted installation and a real mailbox to exercise
subscriber confirmation. Do not use local **Send invitations** to prepare
subscriptions you intend to invite after moving that data to hosting: its durable
claims still prevent those invitations from being sent again.

For Statuspage, Better Stack and Instatus, the confirmation deadline is
**72 hours from the import review time**, even if you have not sent the
invitation yet. Sending later leaves only the time remaining. Sorry candidates
are held without a confirmation deadline until released after cutover; their
72-hour clock starts at release. Candidates not released **30 days after the
import review time** are deleted with their addresses, as an undo would remove
them; Cutover shows the date as **Release by**. Expired pending subscriptions cannot be
invited; the expiry job deletes their unconfirmed addresses. Cutover shows
eligible, already-claimed and expired counts.

Lamp serves its native public JSON at `/api/public/status`. It does not provide a
provider-shaped JSON compatibility API by default. Cutover lists the selected
source's unsupported API and feed paths. Replace old feed subscriptions with
Lamp's `/feed.atom`; replace source widgets with `/widget.js` and configure the
allowed widget origins in Settings. A source widget keeps calling its old host or
stops working when that host is removed.

Repeating an identical import while its prior job is present is an idempotent
no-op. After a successful undo, the source can be imported again. A record the
undo kept because you changed it stays as you left it: a dry run that names it is
refused and names it, so leave it out of the saved responses to import the rest.
**Undo** under
**Your imports** is conditional: it removes rows created by that import only
when their expected values are still present. Rows changed since import and
confirmed subscribers stay, with their reason shown. Aliases stay for surviving
imported incidents or maintenance and are removed when the imported target is
removed. Undo sends no mail.

Moving from another Lamp page? Download your page data from **Settings → Export and restore** there and
restore the file on the new page; see [Backups and recovery](backups-and-recovery.md#export-your-page-data-from-the-app).

Undo applies to one move-in job; it is not a full installation restore. To
restore a complete Lamp installation from an archive, follow [Backups and
recovery](backups-and-recovery.md). Full restore has its own archive and
empty-destination requirements.

For saved responses, include the unchanged object from `GET /v1/pages/{page_id}` as
`page.json` and the unchanged array from `GET /v1/pages/{page_id}/page_access_groups`
as `page-access-groups.json`. Also upload the unchanged JSON arrays named:
`component-groups.json`, `components.json`, `incidents.json`,
`incidents-scheduled.json`, `subscribers.json` and `incident-templates.json`.
For an unresolved incident, also include its unchanged incident-subscriber array
as `incident-subscribers-<incident_id>.json`. Lamp imports supported email
followers as distinct pending subscriptions to that incident, even when the
address already holds a page subscription. Resolved incidents, quarantined
addresses and unsupported channels are named and skipped. Import sends nothing;
the owner must send invitations, and each recipient must confirm in Lamp. A
public follow form cannot bypass that invitation action.

An optional `incident-template-groups.json` array of group IDs and names supplies
template folder names; embedded template groups also supply names. The documented
management API exposes no group-list read. Without a group name, its source ID
is retained as the folder and the dry run names that change. Include later pages as
`<resource>-2.json`, `<resource>-3.json` and so on. The incidents and scheduled
incidents collections may both contain a maintenance; duplicates are carried
once. Statuspage maintenance windows carry over, but their update messages do
not enter Lamp's maintenance history; the unchanged responses remain in raw
source provenance. API reads use pages of 100 and stop after 50 pages per
resource. In saved-file mode, `components.json` is required, but the reader
cannot establish that the files cover every source page or form a complete page
sequence. Include the unchanged pages from one export set. The reader checks
response shapes and its input limits of 8 MiB total, 5,000 records, 512 KiB per
record and 200 files. It cannot prove that no further source pages exist past
its configured page limit. The other resource files may be omitted.

The subscriber API defaults to `state=active`; Lamp does not request
`state=all`, the `unconfirmed` state or the separate
`/subscribers/unsubscribed` endpoint. For a saved-file import, provide the
default active collection. The saved-row reader cannot reliably reclassify a
hand-picked all-state export, so do not upload one. Non-email and quarantined
rows are skipped. Eligible email rows become pending and need the Lamp
invitation and confirmation described above.

The reader refuses team-member-only pages, IP restrictions and nonempty page-access
groups. Missing or unreadable visibility also refuses the import with a plain
notice. Lamp cannot yet preserve private or audience access; no such source is
imported into its public page. Unsupported subscriber
channels do not move. Components marked `only_show_if_degraded` retain their
conditional visibility in Lamp. The source's `showcase` flag does not set a Lamp
visibility rule.

Postmortems with a valid `postmortem_published_at` become published incident
reports at that original time. Bodies with no publication time stay private,
visible only to operators. The report keeps the full body in Summary; the other
report fields are empty. Markdown and HTML become plain text, keeping paragraphs,
headings, list items, link labels and URLs. Images become text naming the image
and source URL; Lamp never fetches or embeds them. Invalid report bodies or
publication times refuse that report without rejecting an otherwise valid incident.
The dry run counts published, kept-private and refused postmortems separately.
Import sends no postmortem notifications, even when the source requested them.

Incident templates retain their name, title, lifecycle, affected components and
states, folder and notification default. Their first body paragraph becomes
Customer impact and the rest becomes Details; Who is affected names their
components. Oversized wording is retained in full and the dry run names each
field to shorten. Open the imported template in the composer, shorten and save
those fields before applying it. An absent next-update offset stays unset for
the operator to choose. Applying a template fills a private draft and publishes
nothing. The source incident's recorded impact is preserved independently of
component claims and uptime history.

This reader maps the source `/incidents/<id>` path for each imported incident or
maintenance, along with any supplied `shortlink` path. If a source shortlink is
absent, that separate shortlink is unavailable; Lamp does not guess it. A full
shortlink such as `https://stspg.io/abc` remains on
that source-owned host; Lamp can serve `/abc` on your moved hostname only when
that path was supplied and accepted. Keep the original redirect or update the
consumer's link.

The source's `/history.atom` and `/history.rss` paths reach Lamp's feeds.
Statuspage JSON readers use `/api/v2/` on the moved hostname. The old
`/embed/script.js` path serves Lamp's floating notice; allow the embedding
origin in Settings. [Public resources](public-resources.md) documents the
read APIs, native pagination and remaining maintenance compatibility gaps.

Statuspage-format webhook bodies and per-component automation email addresses
are not available yet, and Cutover says so. Until they are, keep webhook
receivers and email-wired monitors pointed at Statuspage, or move them to Lamp's
signed webhooks and [alert intake](alerts-from-monitoring-tools.md).
Cutover lists how running Lamp differs from running Statuspage:

Choose **Sorry**. Use a public page's HTTPS origin for a keyless read, or upload
the unchanged JSON files from the local capture below. For an authenticated read, use the masked API key field or capture locally below
with a hidden prompt or private key file. Lamp uses the key for GET requests only
and never stores it. Only move material intended to be public and unrestricted.
Source visibility, audience rules and private-page access do not transfer.
### Capture an authenticated export locally

In Sorry, open **My Account → API Tokens**. Tokens are user-specific. Find the
page ID in its management UI, then run this command from the Lamp checkout with
the pinned Node version:

```sh
node --experimental-strip-types scripts/sorry-capture.mjs --page-id PAGE_ID --out /absolute/private/path/sorry-export
```

After the complete bounded read succeeds, the command creates a local directory
with mode `0700` and original response files with mode `0600`. It never writes
the API token and refuses a response that reflects it. Responses containing
credentials outside the documented subscriber channel fields are also refused.
SMS / phone, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Chat and legacy Slack channels do
not move. Eligible email subscriptions on the same rows are retained; rows
without an enabled email channel are skipped with a reason. Other channel
values are omitted from every retained record. For a response containing
these values, Lamp retains only its
unchanged-byte hash and size, without original-response custody; sanitized
bytes are never labeled as an original. The local capture files remain
unchanged and can contain channel credentials, so keep them private. Captured files
may contain email addresses: keep them private, outside Git, and remove them
when no longer needed. Capture sends no mail and imports nothing. A failed
capture is not an export to import.
Upload the files together in Move in:

The public reader gets `/api/v1/status`, every component and notice collection
page, and `/api/v1/notices/ID` for each notice. Collections expose up to 25 rows
per page; follow `meta.next_page` until complete, checking `meta.total_count`.
The notice list contains summaries; each detail supplies affected components
and full update history. A status overview or the first notice page alone is
incomplete. Pagination stays on the selected HTTPS origin and collection.
Public capture uses `sorry-status.json` instead of `sorry-page.json`, numbered
collection files such as `sorry-notices-2.json`, and the same detail filenames.
Public JSON provides no subscribers. Every notice's detail is read; a capture
missing one is refused. The capture records its requests in
`sorry-public.metadata.json` beside the folder (`<out>.metadata.json`), not
inside it, so in Move in you can select every `.json` file in the folder at once.
See the [public Status API](https://status.sorryapp.com/api).

Sorry documents no native RSS/Atom feed. If the source HTML advertises an
alternate feed, discover its actual `rel="alternate"` link; a feed is a
supplementary discovery source, not proof of a complete history or subscriber
export. Do not guess a feed endpoint or treat a recent feed window as the
archive. Replace existing feed readers with Lamp's `/feed.atom` and JSON readers
with `/api/public/status`. See Sorry's [feed and notification comparison](https://www.sorryapp.com/compare/sorry-vs-statuspage/notifications/).

The dry run reports native mappings, unsupported records and any changes to
source meaning. Canceled maintenance remains canceled and never acquires
a maintenance claim. General notices become resolved informational incidents,
including notices without affected components. In particular, authenticated update text may not include a
lifecycle state for each update; any lifecycle projection is disclosed as a
change, not presented as source evidence. Supplied public notice URLs provide
old-link paths. A path works on a hostname moved to Lamp; Sorry-owned hosts
remain outside Lamp's control. Review the actual destinations in Cutover.

While a Sorry import is retained, `/history`, `/notices` and Sorry's
`/history/YYYY/month` URLs (English month names, such as
`/history/2026/october`) redirect permanently to Lamp's history at `/history/`.
These answers and the history document come from the same public snapshot as
notice redirects. Complete undo removes the Sorry aliases and restores Lamp's
ordinary `/history` document.

Switch the intended hostname using [the custom-domain guide](domains.md), check
that Lamp serves it, and finish the observation window you chose for the move.
Keep Sorry available during this period. In Cutover, use that exact configured
public origin and explicitly confirm both that the hostname is live and that
the observation window has ended before **Send invitations**. Selecting an
origin alone does not verify DNS or finish the observation window.

Choose **Better Stack**. In Better Stack, open **API tokens → Team-based tokens**,
select the team that owns the page, then create or copy an **Uptime API token**
from that team's Uptime section. The [API token settings](https://betterstack.com/settings/api-tokens/0)
and [official token guide](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/getting-started-with-uptime-api/)
show the account controls.

Paste the token into Move in and choose **Find my pages**. Lamp lists the
status pages that token can read, with each page's name, address and ID; choose
**Use this page** beside yours to fill the page ID. (Lamp reads that list from
Better Stack's [List status pages](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/list-all-existing-status-pages/)
API.) The page ID is not a monitor ID or the public hostname.
Enter that page ID and **API token**, or upload the saved original JSON files. Lamp reads from
`https://incidents.betterstack.com/api/v2` using Bearer authentication and `GET`
only; the token is not saved, redirects are refused, and requests stay within
the selected page and report. See the [official status-page API reference](https://betterstack.com/docs/uptime/api/list-all-existing-status-pages/).
Every section, resource, report and subscriber page must be present. Each
report needs its complete update timeline, supplied through update pages or a
matching report detail response. The reader refuses collections over 8 MiB,
5,000 records, 200 files or 50 pages per list rather than importing a truncated
source.

Sections become groups. Displayed resource IDs identify components; underlying
monitor IDs do not. Known operational, degraded, downtime and maintenance
states map to Lamp; paused `not_monitored` or unknown states are refused.
Current non-operational resource states become standing claims at review time.
Historical daily availability aggregates, monitor integrations and widgets
remain source provenance, not invented incidents. Reports retain their
messages, publication times and affected resource states. Because the source
REST report has no investigation lifecycle, Lamp projects Investigating for
affected updates and Resolved for all-resolved updates or the final update of an
ended report. That projection is not a claim about the source lifecycle.
Maintenance windows need a valid end; supplied history appears on the owner
record and public maintenance page without native lifecycle notices, feed
notices or notification jobs.

Only email rows with a valid source confirmation time become pending
subscriptions. Unconfirmed, missing or invalid confirmation, declared
unsubscribed and unsupported channel rows are skipped with reasons. Missing
preferences or unresolved selected resource IDs are never broadened to all
components; an empty explicit selection means all. Existing subscriptions and
suppressions are preserved. The endpoint does not export a complete unsubscribe
ledger, so the dry run cannot account for rows absent from that API response.

The source hostname stays with its owner. Cutover shows only exact supplied
links, the `/feed.atom` feed and the unsupported `/feed.rss` and `/index.json`
readers. Update feed and API readers to Lamp's Atom feed and native
`/api/public/status` endpoint. Source widgets need the same replacement described
above.

Better Stack uses its own source namespace with the same dry run, journal,
revision checks, batching and conditional undo. The additive maintenance-history
migration is included in a full installation backup and restore; a complete
undo removes its unchanged historical messages with the imported maintenance
record.

Choose **Instatus**. In your [Instatus dashboard](https://dashboard.instatus.com),
right-click the project name at the top left and choose **Copy Project ID**;
that value is the **page ID** Lamp asks for. Or paste your API key into Move in
and choose **Find my pages**, then **Use this page** beside yours. Open **User settings → Developer
settings** (or [Developer settings](https://dashboard.instatus.com/developer))
to copy your **API key**. See the [official API help](https://instatus.com/help/api).

Enter the page ID for saved files or an API read. For an API read, also enter
the **API key**. Lamp uses fixed-origin `GET` requests to
`https://api.instatus.com`; it does not save the key or forward it through a
redirect. It selects the requested page from `/v2/pages`, then reads components,
incidents with embedded updates, maintenance lists and each maintenance's
detail, subscribers and audience groups. Saved files require the selected page
ID but no API key. The reader refuses incomplete
collections and input over 8 MiB, 5,000 records, 512 KiB per record, 200 files
or 50 pages per list; it never silently truncates a collection. See
[Instatus API help](https://instatus.com/help/api).

Empty component, incident, maintenance, subscriber and audience-group resources
still need their empty `[]` response; the pages response must contain the
selected page. Maintenance detail is required because the list does not
establish affected components. The optional
`instatus-summary.json` can preserve exact public links supplied for a record;
it is not a complete history export. The API help uses v2 component and
maintenance lists while the official OpenAPI attaches their schemas to v1
reads; check your dry run for missing or refused records before importing.

During Instatus normalization, a missing component or visual-group `createdAt`
uses the selected page's `createdAt`, or `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z` if that is
also absent. A missing component or group `order` defaults to `0`. This
timestamp is a source-normalization default; Lamp timestamps native groups at
import time.

Incident update chronology uses `started`, preserving supplied creation
metadata separately. Maintenance uses its explicit end, or an end derived from
documented duration minutes when completed or configured to end automatically.
Missing or contradictory required ends are refused. Every maintenance update
is retained as history without lifecycle notices or replayed notifications.

Only confirmed, approved, email-only subscribers become pending. Unconfirmed,
unapproved, unsubscribed or deleted rows and unsupported phone, webhook or chat
subscriptions are skipped with reasons. Component preferences must resolve
and are never widened. Capability fields such as tokens, component automation
addresses and webhook credentials are omitted from retained source records.

The optional summary file preserves exact supplied public URLs from
`activeIncidents`, `activeMaintenances` and `recentlyResolvedIncidents`, matched
to management records by source ID. A summary is not complete history. Old URLs
missing from it are unavailable; Lamp never guesses a path or host. Supplied
incident and maintenance paths redirect to surviving Lamp records. The source's
`/history.atom` and `/history.rss` paths reach Lamp's feeds. `/summary.json`,
`/v3/summary.json` and `/v3/components.json` are unsupported. Update JSON readers
to Lamp's native `/api/public/v1/` format. The source hostname
remains outside Lamp's control.

An installation with RER's owner-claim trust configured can enable **Allow
Business imports** in Settings → Export and restore. It starts off; uploads and every other
`/api/rer/import/` route return 404 until enabled. When RER sets the app up for a
Business plan, it also sets `RER_IMPORT_DOOR=on`, and the owner's first claim turns
the door on (Lamp still claims its owner with the setup token there). The owner can
turn it off and on again in the same settings row; a later claim or sign-in never
reopens a door the owner turned off. `rer deploy` never sets the variable, so a
self-hosted Lamp's door stays off until its owner turns it on. The trusted grant key selector
in that same settings row permanently revokes a key immediately. Re-enabling the
door does not restore a revoked key; provisioning must rotate to a new key id.
The door uses the same installation id, issuer, app origin, configured owner email
and ES256 public keys as owner-claim. It never accepts an operator cookie as an
import grant.

Business uploads the same UTF-8 JSON envelope as Move in: `source`
(`statuspage`, `betterstack`, `instatus` or `sorry`), `files` (the unchanged
saved responses as `{name,text}`), and the same optional `pageId`,
`publicAccessAcknowledged` and `publicUrl` fields as Lamp's move-in form. The
grant namespace equals `source`. The saved responses must fit Lamp's 8 MiB /
5,000 record limits; the envelope, which carries them as JSON text, may take
16 MiB. Upload chunks, per-action
grants, plan fingerprints, reconciliation and bounded undo follow the
[Base door protocol](../modules/import-kit/src/door/README.md). Original bytes
stay in this installation.

Lamp's door accepts the four sources Move in offers, `statuspage`,
`betterstack`, `instatus` and `sorry`, one namespace each, on one server-owned
allow-list shared with the owner's Move in: a grant for any other answers 403
`unknown_import_source` (Move in answers 400) before anything is stored. An
apply that fails ends that plan, which says why in **Your imports**; plan the
upload again and approve its new fingerprint. A plan applies within 30 minutes
of its dry run, as Move in's does: after that its apply, and a plan of the same
upload, answer 409 "This dry run has expired. Run the dry run again." (the plan
refusal names the expired `planId`) and store nothing; undo that plan, then plan
the upload again. A request too large for one
request's D1 reads answers 413 `import_door_too_large` and writes nothing.

A later upload to the same namespace is a catch-up. Records whose saved
responses did not change stay as they are, including the subscribers and
templates that namespace already brought in. A changed record is replaced in
place, keeping its id, public reference and display order, unless you edited it
in Lamp: then it is kept and listed as a conflict. Each catch-up also replaces
the namespace's source record, which names the saved responses and review time
it came from. Under a standing (bounded) Business approval, a catch-up is
admitted only when it adds or replaces unedited records and changes under 5% of
the previous snapshot; anything else needs a separate owner review.

When a move is done, Business keeps the old tool's final export with the door's
`archive` action (in this installation's database, as `business-archive/<tool>/<time>`)
and proves it restores with `restore-check`, which reads the archive with the same
readers and writes nothing to the page. Both are grant only, and an erasure
withdraws the archive's bytes as it does the door's other content.

While Business moves a page to Lamp it checks the move with one signed read,
`POST /api/rer/cutover-status`, on the same trust: an RER grant of action
`cutover-status` under the owner-claim keys, refused 403 for a revoked key,
another action, installation or owner, or an expired grant, 401 without a grant,
405 for anything but POST, and 404 when RER's trust is not configured. It reads
and changes nothing else. Given `{since}` (an ISO time) it answers counts and ids
only: the old addresses Cutover lists (their total and up to 25 `{path, target}`
pairs), how many components, incidents and maintenance windows Lamp holds,
subscribers held for cutover and pending, invitations sent since, incidents,
maintenance and subscribers created in Lamp since (imported records excluded), and
each alert source's id, kind and receipts since. It never returns a name, title,
address or secret.

For a public Sorry page, Business can also have Lamp read the page for it:
`POST /api/rer/source-capture`, on the same trust and only while Business imports
are on. It takes an RER grant of action `source-capture` under the owner-claim
keys (401 without a grant, 403 for a revoked key, another action, installation or
owner, or an expired grant, 405 for anything but POST, 404 when RER's trust is not
configured and 404 `import_door_off` while Business imports are off) and
`{"source":"sorry","publicUrl":"https://<host>","maxBytes":<1 to 16777216>}`, at
most 4 KiB. Lamp reads the page keylessly, as **Run dry run** on a public page
does: four fixed GET paths on that origin, no credential, no redirect followed, at
most 120 s and `maxBytes` of responses. It checks the answer with its own Sorry
reader, then answers the bundle the door's `uploads` and `plan` take
(`source`, `publicUrl`, `publicAccessAcknowledged: true`, `files`). A refusal is
`{"error":<code>}` alone: `source_restricted` (409, a private, password, SSO,
unpublished or audience-scoped page), `source_invalid` (422), `source_unreachable`
(502), `capture_too_large` (413), `capture_timeout` (504) or `invalid_capture`
(400). It never writes: no record, upload, plan, nonce or setting changes, and
nothing is logged about the page. The dry run and your review still come before
any import. Managed hosting answers it: this keyless read is the one outbound
read it makes, with Move in's.

Subscribers from every source arriving through Business are held without
invitations until cutover. In Cutover, select the configured live public hostname
and explicitly confirm that it is live and the watch window has closed before
**Send invitations**. That separate owner action starts the existing 72-hour
confirmation window. Unreleased held subscribers expire after 30 days. Undo
cannot recall an invitation already sent. Imported history never queues notices.

After building the candidate, `pnpm sorry:receipt --capture /unchanged/capture --key-file /private/test.pem --out /new/output` (reading the request metadata from `/unchanged/capture.metadata.json`) verifies a public capture in a disposable test installation and signs its receipt; reviewed receipts live in `docs/receipts/` and their public keys belong only in the consumer's test trust store.

1. Sign in and open **Settings → Move in** (`/app/move-in`). Choose the matching
   source in the **Source** menu; its source-specific instructions are below.
2. Enter the source page ID and API key or token where supported, or upload saved provider JSON.
   Credential reads use fixed provider origins and `GET` requests only. Keys are
   used for that read, are not stored, and are not forwarded through redirects.
   Sorry's authenticated export runs locally as described below; its key never
   enters Lamp's Worker.
3. Choose **Run dry run**. Nothing has been written. Review the read, imported,
   changed, skipped and refused counts and the reason for every non-imported row.
   You can download the exact responses read and use those saved files later.
4. Check the review box and choose **Import**. Large imports may pause in batches;
   choose **Continue** until the job is complete. This does not send mail.
5. Open **Settings → Cutover** (`/app/cutover`). Before import it shows proposed
   destinations; after import it shows surviving records. Review the first 25 old
   public addresses, the total address count, unavailable links, reader gaps and
   eligible invitation count.
6. Choose **Send invitations** in Cutover. This is the only move-in action that
   sends mail. It sends one invitation to each eligible pending email subscriber;
   repeat for any remaining batch before the confirmation deadline.
   For Sorry, complete the hostname switch and observation window first; its
   imported subscriber candidates are held until that readiness check, for at
   most 30 days.
7. Point a hostname you control to Lamp using [the custom-domain guide](domains.md),
   or keep the deployment's default public address. Select that public origin in
   Cutover. Selecting it records your choice; it does not check DNS.
8. After switching, use **Check opens** for the listed links. These checks run in
   your browser without cookies or credentials, follow redirects and confirm a
   successful HTML page at the exact Lamp destination. A network, CORS or browser
   access error does not prove that a link works or that it is broken.
9. Keep the old page available through the pending subscribers' confirmation
   deadlines. Update old links, feeds, widgets and API readers before retiring it.

Move in, `rer` and Business imports share one import door. **Run dry run**
uploads the saved responses, unchanged, as one JSON envelope (`source`, `files`
and the form's `pageId`, `publicAccessAcknowledged` and `publicUrl`) to the
door's owner surface, `/api/operator/import/*`, as the signed-in owner, and
shows the door's plan; a key or public page is first read into saved responses
(`POST /api/app/statuspage-import/fetch`, which writes nothing). **Import**
applies exactly the fingerprint you reviewed, in bounded steps. A later import
of the same source is that import's catch-up (see below), and selecting the same
files again reads as already imported. A new dry run replaces one you did not
import. Importing again a source whose import you undid uploads it afresh,
apart from records that undo kept because you changed them in Lamp (see
[Repeat, undo and full-install restore](#repeat-undo-and-full-install-restore)).
A dry run plans the page as it is at that moment and imports for 30 minutes;
after that **Import** answers "This dry run has expired. Run the dry run again."
and changes nothing. **Your imports** lists your imports ("approved by") and Business imports
("approved via Business by") together; undo the newest import of a source first.
Imports made before the door keep their own read, Continue and Undo.

When setup finds the Statuspage, Instatus or Better Stack page your site links to
(or one at `status.<your domain>` that names your site), **Bring its incident history too** reads that
page's public feeds once more, keyless, and imports them through the same door:
Statuspage's `/api/v2/summary.json` and `/api/v2/incidents.json` (its 50 newest
incidents), Instatus's `/summary.json`, `/v2/components.json` and `/history.atom`,
and Better Stack's `/index.json` and `/feed`. The envelope's `files` are those
responses, and `components` lists the components you kept at setup, by the page's
own IDs, with your names. Only resolved incidents come, each update at its original
time; nothing still open on the page, no maintenance and no subscribers. Component
states come only where the feeds state them (Statuspage updates, and the reports a
Better Stack page still shows); any other incident is history that names the
components it lists, without changing their history. An incident about components
you left out stays out. **Your imports** lists the import, and Undo removes it.
A full Move in of the same page later, with its key or saved responses, is that
import's catch-up (see below): the history it brought is replaced in place unless
you changed it in Lamp, nothing it holds is imported again, and what setup did not
bring (maintenance, subscribers, the components you left out) is added without
notifying anyone.
## What saved API responses means

These are `.json` files containing the records your old provider returned when
its API was asked for components, incidents or subscribers. They are not
screenshots, CSV exports or a browser's saved public web page. Upload the files
unchanged and together; Lamp reads them without using an API key. Instatus also
needs the page ID so it can select the right page from those files.

If you have no such files, use the source account/API option in Move in, or ask
the person managing your old status page to capture them using the provider
instructions below. **Download these saved responses** after a dry run also gives you
files you can use for a later saved-response import. Keep them private: subscriber
files can contain personal information. Do not put them in Git.

Lamp serves its native public JSON at `/api/public/status`. It does not provide a
provider-shaped JSON compatibility API by default. Cutover lists the selected
source's unsupported API and feed paths. Replace old feed subscriptions with
Lamp's `/feed.atom`; replace source widgets with `/widget.js` and configure the
allowed widget origins in Settings. A source widget keeps calling its old host or
stops working when that host is removed.

Repeating an identical import while its prior job is present is an idempotent
no-op. After a successful undo, the source can be imported again. A record the
undo kept because you changed it stays as you left it: a dry run that names it is

### Public JSON and feeds

The public reader gets `/api/v1/status`, every component and notice collection
page, and `/api/v1/notices/ID` for each notice. Collections expose up to 25 rows
per page; follow `meta.next_page` until complete, checking `meta.total_count`.
The notice list contains summaries; each detail supplies affected components
and full update history. A status overview or the first notice page alone is
incomplete. Pagination stays on the selected HTTPS origin and collection.
Public capture uses `sorry-status.json` instead of `sorry-page.json`, numbered
collection files such as `sorry-notices-2.json`, and the same detail filenames.
Public JSON provides no subscribers. Every notice's detail is read; a capture
missing one is refused. The capture records its requests in
`sorry-public.metadata.json` beside the folder (`<out>.metadata.json`), not
inside it, so in Move in you can select every `.json` file in the folder at once.
See the [public Status API](https://status.sorryapp.com/api).

Business uploads the same UTF-8 JSON envelope as Move in: `source`
(`statuspage`, `betterstack`, `instatus` or `sorry`), `files` (the unchanged
saved responses as `{name,text}`), and the same optional `pageId`,
`publicAccessAcknowledged` and `publicUrl` fields as Lamp's move-in form. The
grant namespace equals `source`. The saved responses must fit Lamp's 8 MiB /
5,000 record limits; the envelope, which carries them as JSON text, may take
16 MiB. Upload chunks, per-action
grants, plan fingerprints, reconciliation and bounded undo follow the
[Base door protocol](../modules/import-kit/src/door/README.md). Original bytes
stay in this installation.

A later upload to the same namespace is a catch-up. Records whose saved
responses did not change stay as they are, including the subscribers and
templates that namespace already brought in. A changed record is replaced in
place, keeping its id, public reference and display order, unless you edited it
in Lamp: then it is kept and listed as a conflict. Each catch-up also replaces
the namespace's source record, which names the saved responses and review time
it came from. Under a standing (bounded) Business approval, a catch-up is
admitted only when it adds or replaces unedited records and changes under 5% of
the previous snapshot; anything else needs a separate owner review.

When a move is done, Business keeps the old tool's final export with the door's
`archive` action (in this installation's database, as `business-archive/<tool>/<time>`)
and proves it restores with `restore-check`, which reads the archive with the same
readers and writes nothing to the page. Both are grant only, and an erasure
withdraws the archive's bytes as it does the door's other content.

For a public Sorry page, Business can also have Lamp read the page for it:
`POST /api/rer/source-capture`, on the same trust and only while Business imports
are on. It takes an RER grant of action `source-capture` under the owner-claim
keys (401 without a grant, 403 for a revoked key, another action, installation or
owner, or an expired grant, 405 for anything but POST, 404 when RER's trust is not
configured and 404 `import_door_off` while Business imports are off) and
`{"source":"sorry","publicUrl":"https://<host>","maxBytes":<1 to 16777216>}`, at
most 4 KiB. Lamp reads the page keylessly, as **Run dry run** on a public page
does: four fixed GET paths on that origin, no credential, no redirect followed, at
most 120 s and `maxBytes` of responses. It checks the answer with its own Sorry
reader, then answers the bundle the door's `uploads` and `plan` take
(`source`, `publicUrl`, `publicAccessAcknowledged: true`, `files`). A refusal is
`{"error":<code>}` alone: `source_restricted` (409, a private, password, SSO,
unpublished or audience-scoped page), `source_invalid` (422), `source_unreachable`
(502), `capture_too_large` (413), `capture_timeout` (504) or `invalid_capture`
(400). It never writes: no record, upload, plan, nonce or setting changes, and
nothing is logged about the page. The dry run and your review still come before
any import. Managed hosting answers it: this keyless read is the one outbound
read it makes, with Move in's.

1. Sign in and open **Settings → Move in** (`/app/move-in`). Choose the matching
   source in the **Source** menu; its source-specific instructions are below.
2. Enter the source page ID and API key or token where supported, or upload saved provider JSON.
   Credential reads use fixed provider origins and `GET` requests only. Keys are
   used for that read, are not stored, and are not forwarded through redirects.
   Sorry's authenticated export runs locally as described below; its key never
   enters Lamp's Worker.
3. Choose **Run dry run**. Nothing has been written. Review the read, imported,
   changed, skipped and refused counts and the reason for every non-imported row.
   You can download the exact responses read and use those saved files later.
4. Check the review box and choose **Import**. Large imports may pause in batches;
   choose **Continue** until the job is complete. This does not send mail.
5. Open **Settings → Cutover** (`/app/cutover`). Before import it shows proposed
   destinations; after import it shows surviving records. Review the first 25 old
   public addresses, the total address count, unavailable links, reader gaps and
   eligible invitation count.
6. Choose **Send invitations** in Cutover. This is the only move-in action that
   sends mail. It sends one invitation to each eligible pending email subscriber;
   repeat for any remaining batch before the confirmation deadline.
   For Sorry, complete the hostname switch and observation window first; its
   imported subscriber candidates are held until that readiness check, for at
   most 30 days.
7. Point a hostname you control to Lamp using [the custom-domain guide](domains.md),
   or keep the deployment's default public address. Select that public origin in
   Cutover. Selecting it records your choice; it does not check DNS.
8. After switching, use **Check opens** for the listed links. These checks run in
   your browser without cookies or credentials, follow redirects and confirm a
   successful HTML page at the exact Lamp destination. A network, CORS or browser
   access error does not prove that a link works or that it is broken.
9. Keep the old page available through the pending subscribers' confirmation
   deadlines. Update old links, feeds, widgets and API readers before retiring it.

apart from records that undo kept because you changed them in Lamp (see

after that **Import** answers "This dry run has expired. Run the dry run again."
and changes nothing. **Your imports** lists your imports ("approved by") and Business imports

value.meaning: The coordination Worker can read its database; this is not a paging delivery guarantee.

setup.effects: Build and migrate local state, save the first owner and private settings, and retain existing owner, secrets and data on repeat setup. No provider request.

dev.effects: Run Oncall on a loopback address, applying local migrations and printing a private RER_OPEN owner entry. First launch confirms the read-only owner at /setup; later launches open the app. --as signed-out selects the signed-out persona; --login retains automatic owner entry for compatibility. Ordinary /signin email sign-in sends only through a configured remote mail provider with real credentials; no sender is configured by default. --stop stops the owned server.

preview.effects: Serve the built Oncall app on a loopback address with local state and owner sign-in. Ordinary /signin email sign-in sends only through a configured remote mail provider with real credentials; no sender is configured by default. --stop stops the owned server.

deploy.effects: Deploy incident coordination to your own Cloudflare account, claim the configured owner and retire its one-time setup token. Requires Cloudflare credentials and configured remote sign-in mail. Paging stays OFF; keep your existing pager active. --remove --yes deletes owned resources and reads back their absence. --site publishes the separate Run site. --dry-run builds and validates a local plan without credentials or Cloudflare requests and changes nothing remotely. It does not check target secrets, deployment permissions, remote readiness or mail delivery. --site --dry-run builds the separate Run site with no provider request.

export.effects: Write a private local archive of supported durable records and import journal; exclude sessions, credentials and private settings. Stop dev and preview first.

import.effects: Require an empty local destination and explicit --yes; atomically restore validated records and journal, pause pending timers, hold handoff approvals and disable Business import intake. Credentials and sessions never transfer; new owners must explicitly map an archived administrator identity.

demo.effects: A throwaway demo of this seed (rer dev --demo): fresh data in .rer/demo/START (deleted when it stops: --stop, Ctrl-C or its end, one hour by default or --idle-timeout), the saved owner signed in through the demo persona, a separate RER_OWNER_OPEN link for single-use native owner entry on loopback (15-minute expiry; never saved), the seed's demo data, Demo in the app name and title, real public reads/checks and simulated external writes (RER_DEMO=1; the checkout's own data is never touched).

adopt-edition.effects: Add edition.json and sources.lock.json for the existing tracked local source, preserving declared project identity and existing copy/composition records. Create an empty base-copies.json only when none exists. Review and stage the new authoring inputs; no source regeneration, install setup or commit.

refresh-base.effects: Consent to each declared edition edit with repeatable --edition-migration ID; refresh leaves the edit owed. Refresh recorded Base copies to --ref FULL_COMMIT, preserving acknowledged adaptations and applied migrations; announce removed singleton retirement. Deliver invoked workflow helpers atomically; adopt tracked known historical Verify templates and preserve divergent workflows with adoption notices. Acquire committed source from the declared Base repository (default https://github.com/runeditrun/base.git), or read immutable trees, blobs and ancestry through authenticated gh with --from-api, or use --base CHECKOUT or --base-archive DIRECTORY with --ref FULL_COMMIT for an exported source tree. --offline requires --base or --base-archive and never acquires remote source. Refuse incomplete Git checkouts without changing their records. Review the diff and run edition tests before committing.

signin.effects: A one-time sign-in link for the hosted owner, without mail. Uses the Cloudflare credentials that deployed --environment (default production; from the environment or --env-file) to write a single-use grant for the recorded owner into that deployment's auth database, then prints the link once to this terminal; it is never saved. The link works once, only for that owner, expires within 15 minutes, and its use is recorded in the owner's audit log. Signed in this way, the owner can correct a wrong email in settings.

size.effects: Statement size against D1's limits, measured in SQLite on this computer with no account or network. D1 refuses a statement at 100 FROM items, counted with every CTE and view reference expanded in place, or at expression depth 100, and local SQLite and Miniflare accept both; rer fails at 90 of either, a margin of 10 because D1 changed how it enforces them without notice on 10 Nov 2026. With no flags it checks every view and trigger statement of the build's D1 migrations (dist/server/wrangler.json). --migrations DIR checks the objects of that migrations directory instead of the build's. --statements FILE checks the statements of FILE ({"statements":[{"name","sql"}]}, the fleet runner's format) against that schema. Each failure is named with both numbers and the start of its SQL. Exit 1 if any statement fails, 0 if none, 3 with no build and no --migrations. --json lists every statement as {name, fromItems, depth, ok}. With a size-check.json at the checkout root (or --declaration FILE, a declaration kept outside it), rer then builds the declared shape at a small and a large size, each in its own disposable local D1 install served as the hosted check serves the build: the owner is signed in with the bootstrap agent-door conformance uses (the setup manifest's owner-claim step, else verification.owner), each table is generated inside D1 by chunked INSERT … SELECT so the schema's own triggers fire, and each declared table is read back. It prints, for each size and table, the declared count, the count read back and the time per phase; a generation error names the size, the table, the row range, SQLite's message and its column, exits 1 and prints no built line for that size. budget.timeoutSeconds bounds both sizes and a timeout names the phase. While it serves installs it takes verify's job-queue slot (--no-queue only in the original CI environment). Then the personas sign in and every declared flow runs on each size, small first, through a rows-read meter wrapped around the Worker's D1 bindings (fetch, scheduled, queue, Durable Objects and waitUntil work; queues are held and queue consumer work is not measured). A flow fails when it reads more rows at large than its ceiling, more at large than at small by over growthPercent of small plus growthRows (unless growth.allowed), answers the wrong status, has a statement refused or failed by local D1, or runs a statement at 90 FROM items or depth; each failure names its rule and the three statements that read the most rows at large. --json carries every flow at both sizes; --write-statements DIR writes small.json and large.json in the fleet runner's statements format. --statements runs the statement check alone. rer verify runs the schema-object check as its last step.

value.value: In **Settings → Move in**, choose **PagerDuty** or **Opsgenie** to read schedules in the app. PagerDuty uses the installation’s optional OAuth app or a read-only key; Opsgenie uses a read-only key. Review writes no imported objects, and Import paused asks once. The app and generated exporter share `src/move-in/collect/` and read the same pages. The private fallback is under **No key? Use the exporter on your computer**, then **How to export from…**. Download **oncall-export.mjs** and save it in Downloads with that exact name, without a `.txt` suffix. The panel explains how to create a read-only provider key and run the tool; the same steps and official references are in [Save your export with the downloadable tool](docs/move-in.md#save-your-export-with-the-downloadable-tool). Use the Oncall installer’s `rer` command in a macOS, Linux or WSL terminal with internet access to your provider. It supplies its own Node.js runtime; no separate Node installation is needed. No npm packages, API client or manual JSON assembly are needed. Calendar and CSV downloads do not contain the required rotation settings.

```sh
rer run --script ./oncall-export.mjs opsgenie
```

```sh
rer run --script ./oncall-export.mjs pagerduty

Original source timing remains in the journal, and no policy is activated. A PagerDuty schedule may also list layers that ended before the one open-ended layer began and have ended by the time of the preview: that layer is mapped and each ended layer is retained as named history in the review, never as concurrent coverage. setup.effects: Validate rer-setup.json answers, write private .dev.vars (0600), build the Worker, apply migrations/core to .wrangler/state, start Orbit briefly, claim the first owner with the private setup token, prepare checkout-key gated sign-in and stop the app. Reruns keep the owner, data and settings bytes.

dev.effects: Serve Orbit through Vite with HMR on the requested loopback origin, run the minute Cron Trigger locally, and print RER_READY, RER_SIGNED_IN and private checkout-key RER_OPEN once /health answers. Local sign-in mail is suppressed.

preview.effects: Serve the fixed production build with one workerd on the saved state and owner; no rebuild while serving.

build.effects: Build the production Worker and assets into dist/ with private local settings moved aside and restored exactly.

verify.effects: Run scripts/verify.mjs: source, boundary and manifest checks, D1 core and delegation suites, typecheck, built-Worker and browser journeys, the rer command journey, the capacity measurement and the fold qualification. Reports executed gates only; see ACCEPTANCE.md.

reset.effects: After explicit confirmation, remove .wrangler/state, .rer/local, .seed/installer and .dev.vars. Source, dependencies, exports and .rer/deploy receipts stay. No remote effect.

deploy.effects: Build locally, then deploy to the owner's Cloudflare account with the Base deploy kit (Worker, D1 and migrations, minute Cron, declared secrets), check /health and claim the first owner. --dry-run validates the declaration and packaged build with no provider request.

export.effects: Write a new owner-only local archive of every Orbit table through Base portability, with a content hash, row counts and exclusions (sessions, sign-in links, collaborator authority, delegation credentials, archive bookkeeping, source secrets). Remote transfer is not supported here; hosted installations use Records > Archive.

import.effects: Validate an archive, restore it atomically into an empty local database and rebuild search indexes. Run setup afterwards with the archived owner email.

doctor.effects: Read-only tool, version, local settings and state placement diagnostics. No provider request.

describe.effects: Describe commands, flags, aliases, effects, pins and local state without running project commands.

check.effects: Read-only structural validation of the seed command contract, aliases, pins, operations descriptor and copied Base sources.

release.effects: Base release producer: clean source release receipt and optional local tag; never pushes or deploys.

demo.effects: A throwaway demo of this seed (rer dev --demo): fresh data in .rer/demo/START (deleted when it stops: --stop, Ctrl-C or its end, one hour by default or --idle-timeout), the saved owner signed in through the demo persona, a separate RER_OWNER_OPEN link for single-use native owner entry on loopback (15-minute expiry; never saved), the seed's demo data, Demo in the app name and title, real public reads/checks and simulated external writes (RER_DEMO=1; the checkout's own data is never touched).

adopt-edition.effects: Add edition.json and sources.lock.json for the existing tracked local source, preserving declared project identity and existing copy/composition records. refresh-base.effects: Consent to each declared edition edit with repeatable --edition-migration ID; refresh leaves the edit owed. Refresh recorded Base copies to --ref FULL_COMMIT, preserving acknowledged adaptations and applied migrations; announce removed singleton retirement. Deliver invoked workflow helpers atomically; adopt tracked known historical Verify templates and preserve divergent workflows with adoption notices. Acquire committed source from the declared Base repository (default https://github.com/runeditrun/base.git), or read immutable trees, blobs and ancestry through authenticated gh with --from-api, or use --base CHECKOUT or --base-archive DIRECTORY with --ref FULL_COMMIT for an exported source tree. --offline requires --base or --base-archive and never acquires remote source. signin.effects: A one-time sign-in link for the hosted owner, without mail. Uses the Cloudflare credentials that deployed --environment (default production; from the environment or --env-file) to write a single-use grant for the recorded owner into that deployment's auth database, then prints the link once to this terminal; it is never saved. The link works once, only for that owner, expires within 15 minutes, and its use is recorded in the owner's audit log. Signed in this way, the owner can correct a wrong email in settings.

size.effects: Statement size against D1's limits, measured in SQLite on this computer with no account or network. D1 refuses a statement at 100 FROM items, counted with every CTE and view reference expanded in place, or at expression depth 100, and local SQLite and Miniflare accept both; rer fails at 90 of either, a margin of 10 because D1 changed how it enforces them without notice on 10 Nov 2026. With no flags it checks every view and trigger statement of the build's D1 migrations (dist/server/wrangler.json). --migrations DIR checks the objects of that migrations directory instead of the build's. --statements FILE checks the statements of FILE ({"statements":[{"name","sql"}]}, the fleet runner's format) against that schema. Each failure is named with both numbers and the start of its SQL. Exit 1 if any statement fails, 0 if none, 3 with no build and no --migrations. --json lists every statement as {name, fromItems, depth, ok}. With a size-check.json at the checkout root (or --declaration FILE, a declaration kept outside it), rer then builds the declared shape at a small and a large size, each in its own disposable local D1 install served as the hosted check serves the build: the owner is signed in with the bootstrap agent-door conformance uses (the setup manifest's owner-claim step, else verification.owner), each table is generated inside D1 by chunked INSERT … SELECT so the schema's own triggers fire, and each declared table is read back. It prints, for each size and table, the declared count, the count read back and the time per phase; a generation error names the size, the table, the row range, SQLite's message and its column, exits 1 and prints no built line for that size. budget.timeoutSeconds bounds both sizes and a timeout names the phase. While it serves installs it takes verify's job-queue slot (--no-queue only in the original CI environment). Then the personas sign in and every declared flow runs on each size, small first, through a rows-read meter wrapped around the Worker's D1 bindings (fetch, scheduled, queue, Durable Objects and waitUntil work; queues are held and queue consumer work is not measured). A flow fails when it reads more rows at large than its ceiling, more at large than at small by over growthPercent of small plus growthRows (unless growth.allowed), answers the wrong status, has a statement refused or failed by local D1, or runs a statement at 90 FROM items or depth; each failure names its rule and the three statements that read the most rows at large. --json carries every flow at both sizes; --write-statements DIR writes small.json and large.json in the fleet runner's statements format. --statements runs the statement check alone. rer verify runs the schema-object check as its last step.

value.value: Open Records, expand the import and export tools, then choose Move in customer records. Choose the source, select CSV files, check which column holds each detail, and run a dry run. Give the import a name, such as “Old CRM”, and use the same name every time you import an updated file from the same place: Orbit then updates the records it imported before instead of adding them twice. Re-importing an unchanged file changes nothing; changed files and records you edited in Orbit always go through a new review and are never silently overwritten.

Orbit accepts up to eight files, 1,000 rows and 2 MB per file, with 100,000 characters per cell. Use UTF-8 CSV, quoted multiline text and unique headers.
