value.name: OWNER_EMAIL
value.label: Owner email
value.help: The first owner uses this address for sign-in. Local development opens signed in without email.

value.name: IDENTITY_PROVIDER
value.label: Identity provider
value.help: Optional Auth install. Leave empty to use email links.

value.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
value.label: Email provider
value.help: Managed hosting configures mail for you. Free and Assisted hosting use your email provider. Local development suppresses mail.

value.name: ALERT_DESTINATIONS
value.label: Alert destinations
value.help: Optional JSON list of mail or webhook destinations, for example [{"id":"team-mail","project":"web-app","label":"Team mail","channel":"mail","recipient":"team@example.com"}]. Webhooks also need the egress service in docs/ALERT-WEBHOOKS.md.

groups.label: Sign-in email
groups.help: Local development suppresses mail. Hosted sign-in requires an email provider or linked Auth installation.

groups.label: Alerts
groups.help: Optional. Alert rules send to the destinations listed here; leave it empty to start without any.

value.meaning: D1 query and Worker availability; deployment identity when deploy-kit supplies it. Does not prove capture completeness or mail delivery.

setup.effects: Build, apply additive local migrations, create the first real owner or preserve the existing owner, request ordinary outbox sign-in, then stop the temporary runtime. Refuse ambiguous legacy stores before changes.

preview.effects: Serve fixed production output, preserve local owner and durable state, stop after idle timeout or explicit stop.

verify.effects: Build and typecheck; run real Worker/D1 product/auth/restore tests, synthetic accessibility and real public-command/browser journeys at 1440 and 390. Includes native signed owner admission and responsive owner editor checks.

reset.effects: Require confirmation; refuse active state; remove only canonical local data, private settings and installer drafts. Preserve source, exports and deploy receipts.

deploy.effects: Dry-run builds and validates with zero provider calls; an explicit owner-authorized deployment uses the owner Cloudflare account and configured mail sender.

export.effects: Export all owned local D1 domain resources through Base portability, including private maps; exclude auth, grants, outbox and transient admission state.

import.effects: Require confirmation and an empty local destination; validate new and legacy archives, then atomically restore via Base portability. Does not recreate grants or owner.

demo.effects: A throwaway demo of this seed (rer dev --demo): fresh data in .rer/demo/START (deleted when it stops: --stop, Ctrl-C or its end, one hour by default or --idle-timeout), the saved owner signed in through the demo persona, a separate RER_OWNER_OPEN link for single-use native owner entry on loopback (15-minute expiry; never saved), the seed's demo data, Demo in the app name and title, real public reads/checks and simulated external writes (RER_DEMO=1; the checkout's own data is never touched).

adopt-edition.effects: Add edition.json and sources.lock.json for the existing tracked local source, preserving declared project identity and existing copy/composition records. Create an empty base-copies.json only when none exists. Review and stage the new authoring inputs; no source regeneration, install setup or commit.

refresh-base.effects: Consent to each declared edition edit with repeatable --edition-migration ID; refresh leaves the edit owed. Refresh recorded Base copies to --ref FULL_COMMIT, preserving acknowledged adaptations and applied migrations; announce removed singleton retirement. Deliver invoked workflow helpers atomically; adopt tracked known historical Verify templates and preserve divergent workflows with adoption notices. Acquire committed source from the declared Base repository (default https://github.com/runeditrun/base.git), or read immutable trees, blobs and ancestry through authenticated gh with --from-api, or use --base CHECKOUT or --base-archive DIRECTORY with --ref FULL_COMMIT for an exported source tree. --offline requires --base or --base-archive and never acquires remote source. Refuse incomplete Git checkouts without changing their records. Review the diff and run edition tests before committing.

signin.effects: A one-time sign-in link for the hosted owner, without mail. Uses the Cloudflare credentials that deployed --environment (default production; from the environment or --env-file) to write a single-use grant for the recorded owner into that deployment's auth database, then prints the link once to this terminal; it is never saved. The link works once, only for that owner, expires within 15 minutes, and its use is recorded in the owner's audit log. Signed in this way, the owner can correct a wrong email in settings.

size.effects: Statement size against D1's limits, measured in SQLite on this computer with no account or network. D1 refuses a statement at 100 FROM items, counted with every CTE and view reference expanded in place, or at expression depth 100, and local SQLite and Miniflare accept both; rer fails at 90 of either, a margin of 10 because D1 changed how it enforces them without notice on 10 Nov 2026. With no flags it checks every view and trigger statement of the build's D1 migrations (dist/server/wrangler.json). --migrations DIR checks the objects of that migrations directory instead of the build's. --statements FILE checks the statements of FILE ({"statements":[{"name","sql"}]}, the fleet runner's format) against that schema. Each failure is named with both numbers and the start of its SQL. Exit 1 if any statement fails, 0 if none, 3 with no build and no --migrations. --json lists every statement as {name, fromItems, depth, ok}. With a size-check.json at the checkout root (or --declaration FILE, a declaration kept outside it), rer then builds the declared shape at a small and a large size, each in its own disposable local D1 install served as the hosted check serves the build: the owner is signed in with the bootstrap agent-door conformance uses (the setup manifest's owner-claim step, else verification.owner), each table is generated inside D1 by chunked INSERT … SELECT so the schema's own triggers fire, and each declared table is read back. It prints, for each size and table, the declared count, the count read back and the time per phase; a generation error names the size, the table, the row range, SQLite's message and its column, exits 1 and prints no built line for that size. budget.timeoutSeconds bounds both sizes and a timeout names the phase. While it serves installs it takes verify's job-queue slot (--no-queue only in the original CI environment). Then the personas sign in and every declared flow runs on each size, small first, through a rows-read meter wrapped around the Worker's D1 bindings (fetch, scheduled, queue, Durable Objects and waitUntil work; queues are held and queue consumer work is not measured). A flow fails when it reads more rows at large than its ceiling, more at large than at small by over growthPercent of small plus growthRows (unless growth.allowed), answers the wrong status, has a statement refused or failed by local D1, or runs a statement at 90 FROM items or depth; each failure names its rule and the three statements that read the most rows at large. --json carries every flow at both sizes; --write-statements DIR writes small.json and large.json in the fleet runner's statements format. --statements runs the statement check alone. rer verify runs the schema-object check as its last step.

value.value: This guide covers a buyer-authorized Bugsnag organization export and a separate SDK cutover. The importer reads Bugsnag API records directly, under `bugsnag-org:<organization.id>`. It does not turn them into a Sentry export. Historical import does not send notifications, create credentials or start live capture. Local synthetic evidence does not qualify a real buyer migration; MIG-004 register row R-5 still needs an authorized web and mobile project, reconciled source data and actual cutover evidence.
## Capture the authorized source

Use the owner's authorized access to the [Bugsnag Data Access API](https://docs.bugsnag.com/api/data-access/). Spool's CLI reads a local export and never requests a Bugsnag token or calls Bugsnag. Keep provider credentials in the capture tool's private environment or credential store. Never put tokens, authentication headers or credential-bearing URLs in the export, shell arguments, reports or source control.

Record the chosen organization, projects, absolute UTC start and end times, error states, release stages and event sampling before exporting. Include fixed and ignored errors if they belong in the intended scope. An error's aggregate event count is not a list of event occurrences. Retrieve the intended full event reports, with their exceptions, app and original stack fields. The [official API examples](https://docs.bugsnag.com/api/data-access/examples/) describe filtered error reads and event data requests; the API reference linked from the Data Access guide specifies the available endpoints and permissions.

Capture the raw organization object with `id` and `name`; list its projects, then each project's errors, events and releases. Preserve the documented field names and values without constructing SDK payloads. Exclude credential fields such as project `api_key` and `upload_api_key`, and record their removal in `omissions`; retain the submitted export bytes exactly. Request `full_reports=true` when listing events on an error, or retrieve each full event with `GET /projects/{project_id}/events/{event_id}`. A default event-list response can be a summary, not a complete report. Retain native `exceptions[].stacktrace` records and their original method, file, line and address fields as exported. Record inaccessible records, deleted data, retention gaps, sampling, absent reports and unsupported artifact exports in `omissions`. The [official Data Access v2 schema](https://api.swaggerhub.com/apis/smartbear-public/bugsnag-data-access-api/2) defines these response shapes. An asynchronous event-data export job is not itself an event report; inspect its actual downloaded format before adapting it, and never put a signed download URL in the bundle.

[Bugsnag pagination](https://developer.smartbear.com/bugsnag/docs/data-access-pagination) uses the response `Link` header. Follow the URL marked `rel="next"` verbatim after checking that it remains on the authorized API origin; pagination differs by resource. Select API v2 explicitly and respect the endpoint page limit: releases permit at most ten records per page. Honor provider rate limits and report a failed or truncated capture. Do not infer completion from page length or construct an offset yourself. Preserve the chain in the bundle: the first `cursor` is `null`, each `nextCursor` equals the next page's `cursor`, and the last `nextCursor` is `null`. Use credential-free next-link values as cursor strings. If the chosen export is a subset, describe its selection and source endpoint in `omissions`; do not label a truncated chain complete. Keep any returned total counts separately with the capture evidence; they are not invented event rows.

The owner creates a `spool-bugsnag-org-export` version 1 JSON wrapper around those responses. `projects` has `project: null`; `errors`, `events` and `releases` use the Bugsnag project ID in `project`. `organization` is the raw Bugsnag object, and `response` is an array of raw API records. The wrapper is Spool's import format, not a universal Bugsnag export format. An optional project-scoped `stability` collection carries the documented `GET /projects/{project_id}/stability_trend` response object directly as `response` on one page with both cursors null. Keep its `project_id`, `release_stage_name` and `timeline_points`; do not invent an `id` or flatten it into event rows. The report keeps its daily session counts separate from release aggregates and sampled events, with no inferred crash-free rate.

```json
{
  "format": "spool-bugsnag-org-export",
  "version": 1,
  "organization": { "id": "synthetic-spool-1", "name": "synthetic-spool-1" },
  "window": { "start": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", "end": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z" },
  "collections": [
    { "kind": "projects", "project": null,
      "pages": [{ "cursor": null, "nextCursor": null, "response": [] }] },
    { "kind": "errors", "project": "synthetic-spool-2",
      "pages": [{ "cursor": null, "nextCursor": null, "response": [] }] },
    { "kind": "events", "project": "synthetic-spool-2",
      "pages": [{ "cursor": null, "nextCursor": null, "response": [] }] },
    { "kind": "releases", "project": "synthetic-spool-2",
      "pages": [{ "cursor": null, "nextCursor": null, "response": [] }] }
  ],
  "omissions": ["Empty structural example only; no source history was captured."]
}
```

The complete file is bounded to 2 MiB and 500 source records including the manifest, with at most 100 collections and 100 pages per collection. Every exported project must have error, event and release collections, even when their authorized responses are empty. A rejected oversize export is not a successful full-organization import. Reduce the explicitly declared source window or selection and review the resulting scope. Do not silently split history into overlapping unrelated imports. Protect the file with private permissions, for example `chmod 600 bugsnag-organization.json`, and keep it out of source control. Scrubbed native evidence and privately retained exact originals have different privacy boundaries.

Obtain the current owner session through the installation's existing sign-in flow and place its complete cookie header value in a private environment variable named `SPOOL_OWNER_SESSION`. Do not paste the value into a command or report. Agent, ingest and deploy keys do not authorize an import. The endpoint must be the exact Spool origin: HTTPS outside loopback, no credentials, path, query or fragment. Requests carry the owner's cookie, the exact `Origin` and `X-Import-Source: bugsnag-org:<organization.id>`; redirects are refused.

Use the real organization ID printed by dry run. Upload sends the exact bytes in SHA-256-checked 64 KiB chunks through the existing owner-session import door. Dry run stores private upload and review custody and writes no native projects, releases, issues or events. Review its source counts, rejections, omissions, unmapped fields and proposed native differences. Apply requires the plan ID and the exact reviewed 64-character fingerprint; it performs up to 100 bounded requests. If interrupted, `resume` is an alias for `apply` and requires the same organization, plan and reviewed fingerprint. It never silently approves a changed plan.

For a newer capture of the same organization, use `dry-run --catchup`, inspect the changes and review the new fingerprint before applying. Status and reconciliation use the saved plan ID. Reconcile the admitted historical subset against source-ID dispositions and native values; explain every rejected or omitted record before cutover. Review source deletion differences explicitly. Keep the capture window, API totals and sampling evidence beside the report: a successful subset reconciliation does not prove vendor-wide completeness.

Undo the newest import first. Undo checks native row fences and stops on conflicting native edits. Inspect the conflict and deliberately resolve it or keep the import; do not bypass the guard. Reversing imported history does not change an application's SDK configuration or move live events back to Bugsnag. Exact originals and upload custody remain private to this installation; event retention and native archive export are not a complete export or erasure of import custody. See [the shared import door boundaries](SENTRY-SWITCHING.md#review-apply-inspect-and-undo).

Keep exported release stability inputs such as `total_sessions_count` and `unhandled_sessions_count` and their version, stage, time window and semantics as source metadata. If another authorized export exposes `sessions_count`, preserve its documented meaning rather than treating it as an event count. Compare those inputs separately from sampled error and event counts. An omitted or null historical session count means unknown. It must not become zero sessions, inferred sessions, a crash-free percentage or a reconstructed live session stream. Even when a numeric session denominator is exported, it is not equivalent to the sampled imported-event numerator. This importer does not recreate historical sessions or a native release-health dashboard.

The preview and reconciliation report are authoritative for the actual bundle. The import journal retains exact authorized source objects privately; that retention does not mean every field becomes native product data.

| Source evidence | Spool behavior and conversion boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Organization and projects | Deterministic Bugsnag-scoped native projects with source lineage; no owner, collaborator account or project credential is created. Organization settings and roles do not become native settings. |
| Errors and triage | Exported error identities become historical issues. `open` maps to open, `fixed` to resolved, and `ignored` or `snoozed` to suppressed. Snooze expiry, assignment, vendor grouping, workflow rules and source resolution semantics are not reproduced. Unsupported states or malformed parents are reported. |
| Events and stacks | The admitted exported subset becomes scrubbed historical exception evidence. Original exported native stack records remain in private source custody. A readable exported location is evidence of the source stack, not proof that Spool decoded a native symbol file. Missing coordinates, unsupported fields and unavailable full reports remain explicit losses. |
| App and releases | App version, stage and build map to release `version@stage+build`, with stage as environment and build as the native build identity. Absent build maps to `unspecified`. Missing or ambiguous required identities are reported; no deployment or latest build is guessed. Compare the actual mapped identity to the SDK configuration before switching. |

| Collaborators and integrations | Authorized records or references may remain private source evidence, with unmapped dispositions. Users, teams, memberships, alert rules, webhooks, notification destinations and external credentials are not activated. |
| Source maps and symbols | Exported artifact references do not contain the corresponding artifact bytes. A reference does not recover a map, dSYM, ProGuard mapping, binary or NDK symbol file. Retain matching artifacts from the original build separately. |
| Other event data | User, request, device, custom metadata, thread details, breadcrumbs and secondary exceptions may exceed the native evidence model; inspect per-record unmapped fields. Exact private originals are broader than the scrubbed issue packet. |
| History and totals | Sampling, provider retention, inaccessible records and unsupported collections stay declared. Native counts describe admitted exported occurrences, not the aggregate vendor counter. Import is inert and creates no live session, alert delivery or SDK capture. |

Before publishing a minified build, register that exact release and upload its matching JavaScript maps with a Spool project deploy key using [Spool's source-map CLI or Vite plugin](SENTRY-SWITCHING.md#register-upload-then-change-the-dsn). Replace the Bugsnag map-upload step with this upload; do not reuse the Bugsnag token. Keep deploy grants in CI secrets and use the documented environment-variable-name option. Keep browser origins exact and preserve the same release, build and debug identity in uploaded maps and captured events. Do not mix map injectors on one bundle.

Trigger a real exception in the deployed web build. Verify its project, version, stage, build and original path, line and column in Spool; a successful SDK flush alone does not prove admission. Record the first live event and the cutover time separately from imported history. Retain the previous deployment configuration for rollback until that evidence is reviewed.

Replace the mobile Bugsnag SDK with the corresponding unmodified Sentry SDK and set the Spool project DSN: [Apple setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/apple/), [Android setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/android/) or [React Native setup](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/react-native/). Replace notify calls, startup hooks and handled-exception capture as required by that SDK. This is a migration recipe, not a claim that every native crash transport or mobile SDK has been qualified against Spool. Check the [current supported-language boundaries](SUPPORTED-LANGUAGES.md) and prove a real device event before treating a mobile switch as complete.

An upload step can read the credential directly from the CI environment without putting its value in shell arguments. Set `SPOOL_ENDPOINT`, `SPOOL_PROJECT`, `SPOOL_RELEASE`, `SPOOL_BUILD`, `SPOOL_MAPPING_FILE` and the secret `SPOOL_DEPLOY_KEY` in CI, then run:

Original filenames require R8 source-file metadata such as `# {"id":"sourceFile","fileName":"MainActivity.kt"}` beneath the class mapping. An original line requires unambiguous explicit line ranges. Ambiguous inlining and absent source metadata remain named gaps; Spool does not invent an original filename or line. Preserve the full build mapping and app identifiers, as the [Bugsnag ProGuard upload guidance](https://docs.bugsnag.com/build-integrations/bugsnag-cli/upload-android-proguard/) also requires for matching.

**Spool does not yet decode these files.** It reads only their identity (Mach-O UUID, ELF build id, architecture). It has no Mach-O/DWARF or ELF symbol reader, and its event frame model keeps no instruction address or module, so a native crash frame is not resolved through a stored file, and no original frame is ever claimed from one. The upload response says `symbolication: unsupported`, and a Bugsnag import dry run reports each project's Mach-O/ELF frames under `nativeStacks` and as a `native_frames` conversion loss. Treat the upload as keeping your debug files with the right project and identity for when decoding exists, not as native symbolication.

For the historical acceptance sample, compare the original exported native frames to the private original and the mapped issue evidence. Record which frames were already readable at source, which coordinates survived, and which remain unavailable. For new Android events, prove the original file and line from the matching uploaded map on a real build. A retained old native stack does not prove a new mobile crash can be decoded. Apple and NDK uploads are stored but native frames are not symbolicated, so that cutover remains incomplete; a synthetic Android pipeline check does not qualify a real buyer device or complete register row R-5.

Capture the raw organization object with `id` and `name`; list its projects, then each project's errors, events and releases. Preserve the documented field names and values without constructing SDK payloads. Exclude credential fields such as project `api_key` and `upload_api_key`, and record their removal in `omissions`; retain the submitted export bytes exactly. Request `full_reports=true` when listing events on an error, or retrieve each full event with `GET /projects/{project_id}/events/{event_id}`. A default event-list response can be a summary, not a complete report. Retain native `exceptions[].stacktrace` records and their original method, file, line and address fields as exported. Record inaccessible records, deleted data, retention gaps, sampling, absent reports and unsupported artifact exports in `omissions`. The [official Data Access v2 schema](https://api.swaggerhub.com/apis/smartbear-public/bugsnag-data-access-api/2) defines these response shapes. An asynchronous event-data export job is not itself an event report; inspect its actual downloaded format before adapting it, and never put a signed download URL in the bundle.

[Bugsnag pagination](https://developer.smartbear.com/bugsnag/docs/data-access-pagination) uses the response `Link` header. Follow the URL marked `rel="next"` verbatim after checking that it remains on the authorized API origin; pagination differs by resource. Select API v2 explicitly and respect the endpoint page limit: releases permit at most ten records per page. Honor provider rate limits and report a failed or truncated capture. Do not infer completion from page length or construct an offset yourself. Preserve the chain in the bundle: the first `cursor` is `null`, each `nextCursor` equals the next page's `cursor`, and the last `nextCursor` is `null`. Use credential-free next-link values as cursor strings. If the chosen export is a subset, describe its selection and source endpoint in `omissions`; do not label a truncated chain complete. Keep any returned total counts separately with the capture evidence; they are not invented event rows.

value.value: ## Capture the source

| Bundle location | Authorized source |
| --- | --- |
| `project` | [Get a project](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get-a-project), `GET /api/1/project/{project_id}`. This endpoint requires an account token with `read` scope. Keep the complete `{err:0,result:{id,...}}` envelope. |
| `items` | [List all items](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/list-all-items), `GET /api/1/items/`. Keep every `result.items` page, including resolved and muted items; do not leave an active-only filter in the capture. |
| `occurrences` | Discover IDs through [list occurrences](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-instances), `GET /api/1/instances`, then capture [each occurrence detail](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-instance-instance-id), `GET /api/1/instance/{instance_id}`. Each bundle page holds one detail response with `result.id`, `result.item_id` and `result.data`, rather than a list summary. |
| `deploys` | [List all deploys](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/list-all-deploys), `GET /api/1/deploys`. Keep the exact envelope with `result.deploys`. |
| `item_events` | [List events for an item](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/list-item-events), `GET /api/1/item/{item_id}/events`, without a type filter. Use the system item ID, not its display counter. Keep comments and history in the raw envelope. |
| `notification_rules`, channel `email` | [Read email rules](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-notifications-email-rules), `GET /api/1/notifications/email/rules`. |
| `notification_rules`, channel `slack` | [Read Slack rules](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-notifications-slack-rules), `GET /api/1/notifications/slack/rules`. |
| `notification_rules`, channel `pagerduty` | [Read PagerDuty rules](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-notifications-pagerduty-rules), `GET /api/1/notifications/pagerduty/rules`. |
| `notification_rules`, channel `webhook` | [Read webhook rules](https://docs.rollbar.com/reference/get_api-1-notifications-webhook-rules), `GET /api/1/notifications/webhook/rules`. |

Follow each endpoint's pagination to exhaustion. Item, deploy and history pages start at 1. Keep the terminal empty page when supplied. For occurrence details, number the captured detail responses consecutively in discovery order. Put `complete: true` on every collection only after exhausting its source. This is your completeness declaration; the importer cannot prove no response was omitted. Do not declare an interrupted or rate-limited capture complete. Quiesce the source for a final capture or record its changing-source limitation before cutover.

```text
{
  format: 'spool-rollbar-export', version: 1, exportedAt: '<ISO timestamp>',
  project: <exact project response envelope>,
  collections: [
    {kind: 'items', complete: true,
      pages: [{page: 1, response: <exact items envelope>}, ...]},
    {kind: 'occurrences', complete: true,
      pages: [{page: 1, response: <exact ONE occurrence detail envelope>}, ...]},
    {kind: 'deploys', complete: true,
      pages: [{page: 1, response: <exact deploys envelope>}, ...]},
    {kind: 'item_events', item: <system item ID>, complete: true,
      pages: [{page: 1, response: <exact events envelope>}, ...]},
    {kind: 'notification_rules', channel: 'email', complete: true,
      pages: [{page: 1, response: <exact rules envelope>}]}
  ],
  unavailable: [{kind: '<missing source category>', reason: '<specific reason>'}]
}
```

Items, occurrences and deploys are required. Empty item and deploy lists retain their successful API envelopes. An exhausted occurrence discovery with no available details uses an empty `pages` array; name unavailable occurrence history when source counters exceed those retained details. Include a separate history collection per item and a separate rules collection per channel captured. Every collection's page numbers must be contiguous from 1. Name each missing history in `unavailable` with `kind: 'item_events'`, its numeric `item` and a reason. Name each missing channel with `kind: 'notification_rules'`, its `channel` and a reason; a denied history request, an unconfigured channel and an unknown artifact download are different gaps. Name source maps, symbol files, attachments and any other artifact whose download was not established as unavailable. Never imply bytes were captured because an occurrence contains a URL or artifact name. Do not manufacture an API response for an unavailable source.

Store the bundle privately with restrictive permissions, outside the repository. Preserve the original capture independently. Credentials found in source data may be removed by the server's existing custody policy; inspect the plan's named refusals and losses before applying.

Sign in as the installation's existing owner. Privately populate `SPOOL_OWNER_COOKIE` with that owner's session cookie through your session tooling. The CLI takes only the environment variable's name; there is no session-value flag. Use an HTTPS origin, or HTTP on loopback for local work. Each POST includes that exact Origin and `X-Import-Source: rollbar-project:<project ID>`; the source ID comes from `String(bundle.project.result.id)`.

The client uploads the exact bundle in checked 64 KiB chunks, with SHA-256 for each chunk and the complete bundle. It verifies completion before requesting a plan. Read the returned `project`, `namespace`, `uploadId`, `planId`, `fingerprint`, counts, differences, rejected records and diagnostics. A dry run retains private custody and planning state but writes no native records. Check that every source identity and every unavailable category is accounted for. Resolve rejections or explicitly accept the reported losses before approving that fingerprint.
Use the project ID, plan ID and exact fingerprint from the reviewed result:

Resume uses the same reviewed apply route; it does not create another plan or bypass fingerprint review. Status reads progress. Reconcile checks native records and provenance against source identities on the server; inspect its dispositions and mismatches before cutover. Undo runs bounded reversal requests, newest snapshot first, under existing native-edit guards. A changed native target can refuse reversal; inspect the refusal instead of overwriting edits. Each loop stops after 100 requests, leaving the server's durable state available for another status check and continuation.

Review the server plan as the authority for each mapped issue, occurrence, frame and deploy-derived release. Rollbar item identity is retained in provenance; Spool's future native grouping need not reproduce Rollbar grouping. Spool accepts bounded JavaScript, Python and Go exception evidence. This is not a claim of Sentry feature parity or a completed customer migration. Organization import is qualified with synthetic fixtures only. An owner-supplied real export must be reconciled before any Sentry-alternative claim.

The Sentry error envelope and legacy store endpoints convert exceptions into Spool's existing admission path: project key, exact browser origin, release handling (see [Sentry release identity](SENTRY-RELEASES.md)), scrubbing, duplicate identity, grouping, bounded storage, diagnosis and alerts. Unsupported items are counted under a fixed taxonomy and discarded. No unsupported payloads are retained. Text feedback from modern feedback events/items and legacy user_report is retained separately under [Text feedback](FEEDBACK.md), with exact occurrence association, owner review and withdrawal. Contact, screenshots and other attachments are excluded. Sessions, tracing/spans, attachments, client reports, replay, profiles, logs and metrics do not become product data. Cron check-ins are never stored as evidence; they are routed to a connected Uptime heartbeat, or counted as unrouted, under [Cron check-ins](CHECK-INS.md).

The full verify runs unmodified `@sentry/browser` and `@sentry/node` 11.6.0 with their default integrations, and one parallel job per server runtime runs an unmodified Sentry SDK program (see [Runtime qualification](#runtime-qualification)). The same program and SDK configuration use a local reference collector DSN and then a Spool DSN; only the DSN changes. Browser capture checks mapped source coordinates at 1440 and 390, and Node capture awaits flush. Exact-head results belong in the completion evidence; package pins alone do not prove runtime behavior. These programs make no Sentry account or service calls.

Transport limits are 256 KiB compressed (gzip or deflate), 1 MiB expanded/uncompressed, 100 envelope items and 8 KiB per header. Item lengths are bytes; zero-length and binary unsupported items are valid. The entire framing is checked before any event is admitted. Supported encodings are identity, gzip and deflate. Unsupported encodings return 415 with the encoding named; header/query-authenticated refusals are counted as `unsupported_content_encoding`. Within a correctly framed envelope at these transport limits, malformed event JSON and deterministic event-conversion failures (including an invalid or disagreeing event ID, conflicting source-map debug IDs and invalid normalized fields) refuse only that event. The response retains `dropped.invalid_item` and adds `refusedItems`, with `type: "event"`, `reason: "invalid_item"` and the exact `quantity`. Existing project outcomes and organization usage count those same `invalid_item` units; each newly admitted companion error consumes one accepted unit and retains one occurrence. Rejected events commit no prepared identity, scrubbing or product writes. Database failures still use the storage-failure response, and invalid legacy `/store/` requests remain whole-request refusals. Constructed-envelope proof in `tests/sentry-invalid-event-flow.mjs` qualifies this conversion boundary only; it does not establish other item categories, larger limits, native-device capture or a real Sentry dual run. Malformed envelope framing and whole-request size failures still reject the whole request. Brotli and zstd remain unsupported. Query auth, `X-Sentry-Auth`, Bearer auth if supplied, and envelope DSN credentials must agree; the protocol version (`sentry_version`) may be 5 to 7, since the Elixir SDK still sends 5. The public key grants ingest only and a numeric DSN project alias is bound to one native project. Invalid, revoked or wrong-project keys and unauthorized browser origins cannot admit events. Ingest keys remain valid until revoked.

The outermost reported exception supplies the stack. Frames are reversed from Sentry's oldest-first order and columns are converted from one-based to zero-based once. Spool keeps frames that have a file and a line (JavaScript frames also need a column; Python/Go may omit it) and skips frames that lack them. An event left with no usable frame is still admitted, with no stack frames. A message-only capture, such as a frameless `Sentry.captureMessage` or an event carrying only `message` or `logentry`, becomes an issue titled `Message: <text>` with type Message, grouped by its message template when the SDK sends one. An exception event with no stack, or with only frames that lack coordinates, becomes an issue titled `<type>: <value>` with no frames. Spool's own native version-1 intake still requires at least one frame. Request/user/context/module/local-variable data is not persisted; selected exception fields and breadcrumb labels pass the existing scrubber. Debug metadata is matched against raw frame paths before query strings and private local paths are removed.

2. Set the SDK `release` (and `dist`, if you use one) to the names your build uploads source maps under. Admission does not need a release registered first. By default the first event that names a release Spool has not seen creates it, as Sentry does, and it shows as **Auto-created** in release history. An event with no `release` field is accepted and stored with release **none**: it counts in issues and search and is left out of per-release figures. A name Sentry itself refuses (empty, `.`, `..`, `latest`, or containing a newline, tab, `/` or `\`, or over 200 characters), and an unseen name outside a project's automatic-release pattern, are accepted as release none with a processing note. Registering the same release later through the release API, `sentry-cli releases` or a build plugin enriches it and removes the label. An absent `dist` has its own internal build identity, separate from a `dist` string that happens to read `sentry-no-dist`. Spool never infers the latest release. One release currently has one build; use distinct release names for distinct distributions.

Registration matters for source maps: an upload for a release Spool has not seen is refused (409) until the release is registered or an earlier event has created it, and a map is used for a frame only on an exact release, build, debug ID and checksum match. Register and upload before publishing so the first events resolve to original source. A project can opt in to **Registered sequence only** in Settings. Then an event with no `release` is refused with `missing_release_register_required`, and a release or build that is not registered is refused with `unregistered_release_or_build`. Both are counted in project outcomes and returned with the registration path.

`npx -p @just-every/spool spool-setup --dsn <project DSN> --dir <app>` detects the framework from the app's own manifests, prints the change as a patch that `git apply` accepts, and writes nothing. Add `--apply` to write exactly that patch, `--install` to run the package install (`--python` and `--spool-package` choose the interpreter and the Spool package spec), and `--no-test-event` to skip the test event. The test event goes through Spool's public intake before anything is printed as a patch or written, and counts as accepted only when the DSN's own host answers with Spool's receipt for it; a refusal, a redirect (never followed) or a host that is not Spool stops the command with nothing written. A DSN with a secret key (`key:secret@`) is refused without being printed or written, and so is one with spaces or control characters; only the canonical `key@host/number` form is written. A file or folder on a path the command writes that is a link (inside the project or out of it), a file to change that has another hard link, and a `DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` that is not a dotted name of ASCII letters, digits and underscores each stop the command before anything is sent or written, and the dry run prints no patch for them (`git apply` likewise refuses a path through a symbolic link). Writing follows no link and changes no file in place: each folder is opened without following links and pinned as the working directory, each change is a new file renamed over its target once the target is checked against the plan (a new file must still be absent; a changed one must be the same single-link file with the same bytes; its permissions are kept), and around each rename the folders are checked to still be where the plan names them. Anything on those paths that changed after the command read the project (during the test event, say) stops it, and changes already made are undone; a change landing between the last check and the rename call itself is replaced, as with `git apply`. `--dir` itself may be a link: it is resolved once. The command needs no-follow file opens, so it runs on macOS, Linux and WSL2, not native Windows. Rerunning is idempotent.

Each tunnel reads the envelope's DSN header and forwards only when it names a DSN the tunnel was configured with; another key, host or project is refused (403) and nothing is forwarded. It forwards the browser's `Origin`, `Referer` and `User-Agent`, so Spool's allowed origins and inbound filters still decide, returns Spool's `X-Sentry-Rate-Limits`, and forwards the client address as `X-Forwarded-For`. Spool does not yet honour a forwarded address from a trusted tunnel (SDK-008), so events carry the tunnel server's own address until it does. A tunnel never follows a redirect: an upstream 3xx is answered with 502 and nothing reaches the host it names. Only `POST` is accepted (anything else is 405, and an abandoned upload ends that request, not the server), and the 1 MiB envelope limit is enforced while the body is read and again while it is inflated, so a small gzip body that expands far past the limit is refused (413) without being expanded. The `tunnel-flow` journey runs a real `@sentry/browser` page and a fresh Next.js app (`next build`, `next start`) under the EasyPrivacy Sentry rules in the Ghostery blocking engine; this is an engine and an excerpt of the list, not a browser extension.

- **Express**: `@sentry/node`; call `Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SPOOL_DSN })` from a file you import first, then `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` after your routes.
- **Django / FastAPI**: `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=os.environ["SPOOL_DSN"])` before the app is created; the Django, FastAPI and Starlette integrations are defaults. Django request data is run through a real WSGI request above.
- **Spring**: `io.sentry:sentry-spring-boot-starter-jakarta` with `sentry.dsn=${SPOOL_DSN}`.
- **Rails**: `sentry-ruby` and `sentry-rails`, `config.dsn = ENV["SPOOL_DSN"]` in an initializer.
- **Laravel**: `sentry/sentry-laravel`, `php artisan sentry:publish --dsn=$SPOOL_DSN`.
- **ASP.NET Core**: the `Sentry.AspNetCore` package and `UseSentry(o => o.Dsn = ...)`.
## Export format and scope

There is no universal Sentry organization JSON export assumed by this importer. The input is an **owner-generated** `spool-sentry-org-export` version 1 bundle of exact paginated API response objects. The local file holds organization ID/slug/region (`us`, `de`, or `self-hosted`), the requested start/end window, declared omissions, and collections for projects, releases, issues and selected event details. All selected pages must form a cursor chain ending in `nextCursor: null`.
An owner with appropriate Sentry read permissions generates it from the official APIs:

- [List organization projects](https://docs.sentry.io/api/organizations/list-an-organizations-projects/).
- [List organization releases](https://docs.sentry.io/api/releases/list-an-organizations-releases/).
- [List project issues](https://docs.sentry.io/api/events/list-a-projects-issues/). Explicitly request all intended states; the default unresolved query is not all history. Follow every pagination cursor in the intended time window.
- [Retrieve event details](https://docs.sentry.io/api/events/retrieve-an-event-for-a-project/). Supply the intended issue events; an issue summary's total count is not an event export. Record any sampling, inaccessible/deleted events, retention gaps and partial windows under `omissions`.

The importer currently bounds a file to 2 MiB, 500 source records and 100 collections/pages per collection. Unsupported collections and fields remain explicitly accounted for as omissions; invalid supported records are shown as rejections. Dry run uploads the exact bytes in SHA-256-checked 64 KiB chunks and returns the plan: its fingerprint, counts, rejected records with reasons, and differences against the organization's previous import. It writes no native records. Apply needs the plan ID and the exact reviewed fingerprint; it repeats bounded requests until the server reports the job `completed`, and repeating it answers the same job. `status` reads the job; `reconcile` re-derives every source ID's disposition (present, or explained with its reason) and the native counts, revisions and values from Spool's data. A newer bundle of an imported organization is a catch-up: add `--catchup` to the dry run; unchanged records stay, changed records it created are proposed as guarded replacements and records gone at source are only listed. One bundle's historical events keep one set of occurrence identities; a different bundle gives fresh ones. Apply and undo check the current owner session in the same SQL transaction as native rows and the Base journal. Undo runs newest import first, in reverse dependency order. Exact full-row fences catch native edits even when a revision number was not advanced; a conflict stops reversal and preserves edits. Restore the conflicting row deliberately or keep the import; never bypass the guard. Settings → **Business imports** lists every import ("approved by" for the owner's own, "approved via Business by" for Business) with an Undo.

The uploaded bytes and each plan's snapshot stay private to this installation, separate from scrubbed issue packets. Project event retention does not erase them. Native owner archives include scrubbed historical rows and source identity metadata but deliberately exclude the import door and Base import journal; undo and reconciliation remain on the installation that holds them. Keep the export file itself confidential; deleting a native event is not erasure of its original export. This release has no automatic source-journal expiry.

Transport limits are 256 KiB compressed (gzip or deflate), 1 MiB expanded/uncompressed, 100 envelope items and 8 KiB per header. Item lengths are bytes; zero-length and binary unsupported items are valid. The entire framing is checked before any event is admitted. Supported encodings are identity, gzip and deflate. Unsupported encodings return 415 with the encoding named; header/query-authenticated refusals are counted as `unsupported_content_encoding`. Within a correctly framed envelope at these transport limits, malformed event JSON and deterministic event-conversion failures (including an invalid or disagreeing event ID, conflicting source-map debug IDs and invalid normalized fields) refuse only that event. The response retains `dropped.invalid_item` and adds `refusedItems`, with `type: "event"`, `reason: "invalid_item"` and the exact `quantity`. Existing project outcomes and organization usage count those same `invalid_item` units; each newly admitted companion error consumes one accepted unit and retains one occurrence. Rejected events commit no prepared identity, scrubbing or product writes. Database failures still use the storage-failure response, and invalid legacy `/store/` requests remain whole-request refusals. Constructed-envelope proof in `tests/sentry-invalid-event-flow.mjs` qualifies this conversion boundary only; it does not establish other item categories, larger limits, native-device capture or a real Sentry dual run. Malformed envelope framing and whole-request size failures still reject the whole request. Brotli and zstd remain unsupported. Query auth, `X-Sentry-Auth`, Bearer auth if supplied, and envelope DSN credentials must agree; the protocol version (`sentry_version`) may be 5 to 7, since the Elixir SDK still sends 5. The public key grants ingest only and a numeric DSN project alias is bound to one native project. Invalid, revoked or wrong-project keys and unauthorized browser origins cannot admit events. Ingest keys remain valid until revoked.

Each bundle requires an adjacent `.map`. This injects the standard Sentry debug registration after the bundle's directive prologue, preserves shebangs and strict/sloppy execution, and adjusts generated line/column mappings with matching `debug_id` metadata. Existing matching identities are reused, identical API retries are idempotent, and conflicting map content or release/build identities reject. Up to twenty flat maps of 256 KiB per project are supported; indexed maps and unbounded artifact bundles are not.

A failed registration or upload fails the build. The deploy secret is never injected. The CLI/plugin are Spool tooling; they do not implement Sentry's artifact-bundle upload API. Do not mix injectors on the same bundle.

import.effects: After confirmation validate Base integrity and atomically restore complete product/history records into an empty destination, with monitors paused, destinations disabled and notifications quarantined.

Uses the Cloudflare credentials that deployed --environment (default production; from the environment or --env-file) to write a single-use grant for the recorded owner into that deployment's auth database, then prints the link once to this terminal; it is never saved. The link works once, only for that owner, expires within 15 minutes, and its use is recorded in the owner's audit log. Signed in this way, the owner can correct a wrong email in settings.

size.effects: Statement size against D1's limits, measured in SQLite on this computer with no account or network. D1 refuses a statement at 100 FROM items, counted with every CTE and view reference expanded in place, or at expression depth 100, and local SQLite and Miniflare accept both; rer fails at 90 of either, a margin of 10 because D1 changed how it enforces them without notice on 10 Nov 2026. With no flags it checks every view and trigger statement of the build's D1 migrations (dist/server/wrangler.json). --migrations DIR checks the objects of that migrations directory instead of the build's. --statements FILE checks the statements of FILE ({"statements":[{"name","sql"}]}, the fleet runner's format) against that schema. Each failure is named with both numbers and the start of its SQL. Exit 1 if any statement fails, 0 if none, 3 with no build and no --migrations. --json lists every statement as {name, fromItems, depth, ok}. With a size-check.json at the checkout root (or --declaration FILE, a declaration kept outside it), rer then builds the declared shape at a small and a large size, each in its own disposable local D1 install served as the hosted check serves the build: the owner is signed in with the bootstrap agent-door conformance uses (the setup manifest's owner-claim step, else verification.owner), each table is generated inside D1 by chunked INSERT … SELECT so the schema's own triggers fire, and each declared table is read back. It prints, for each size and table, the declared count, the count read back and the time per phase; a generation error names the size, the table, the row range, SQLite's message and its column, exits 1 and prints no built line for that size. budget.timeoutSeconds bounds both sizes and a timeout names the phase. While it serves installs it takes verify's job-queue slot (--no-queue only in the original CI environment). Then the personas sign in and every declared flow runs on each size, small first, through a rows-read meter wrapped around the Worker's D1 bindings (fetch, scheduled, queue, Durable Objects and waitUntil work; queues are held and queue consumer work is not measured). A flow fails when it reads more rows at large than its ceiling, more at large than at small by over growthPercent of small plus growthRows (unless growth.allowed), answers the wrong status, has a statement refused or failed by local D1, or runs a statement at 90 FROM items or depth; each failure names its rule and the three statements that read the most rows at large. --json carries every flow at both sizes; --write-statements DIR writes small.json and large.json in the fleet runner's statements format. --statements runs the statement check alone. rer verify runs the schema-object check as its last step.

For a simple URL list instead, use **New monitor › Paste many URLs or a CSV** with Uptime's `url,name,interval` header and intervals in seconds.

Open **New monitor › Import a file** (also available under **Settings › Backup and files**), choose the file or **Paste it instead**, and select **Preview**. **Accepted files and export steps** shows the supported formats, samples and provider guides. Uptime detects the UptimeRobot format; if it cannot, choose it under **Choose the source**. The preview counts entries that are importable, importable with listed differences, and unsupported, then shows each monitor with its notes. Apply creates the importable monitors, paused. You can undo the whole import from the batch list. From a terminal, `node scripts/definitions.mjs preview --input uptimerobot-monitors.json` does the same.

- **HTTP(S) monitors** become HTTP(S) monitors with the same URL and method. UptimeRobot's default method is HEAD; a QUERY method is unsupported.
- **Keyword monitors** keep their condition: alert-when-missing requires the text (`bodyIncludes`), and alert-when-present requires its absence (`bodyExcludes`). Uptime matches the text exactly, so a case-insensitive keyword is listed as a difference for either condition. An unspecified or unrecognised case setting is also named for review before enabling.
- **Expected status codes.** Exact codes, sets and inclusive ranges move without narrowing the accepted responses. For example, `200, 201, 204`, `200-299` and UptimeRobot's default `2xx, 3xx` keep every accepted status. An unrecognised code or range makes the entry unsupported; the importer never replaces it with 200.
- **Timeouts** move in seconds, within Uptime's range of 0.05 to 10 seconds. A longer timeout becomes 10 seconds, and the preview says so.
- **Intervals** move unchanged from seconds to milliseconds. An interval under 5 seconds or over one day is shown with its number and not imported. If an interval ever had to change, the preview would state it as a cadence change.
- **Heartbeat monitors** become Uptime heartbeats that expect a call within the interval plus UptimeRobot's grace period, up to one day in all. When the interval plus grace is longer than one day, such as a daily heartbeat with a grace period, Uptime keeps the interval and shortens the grace so the total is one day; the preview names the original and the shortened numbers. Their old heartbeat URL stops working for Uptime: issue a new token on the monitor's page and repoint your jobs to it. The preview lists the old URL so you know which jobs to change.

Every imported monitor checks from probe `local-a` on your own runner, and its evidence counts as fresh for at least three intervals. Uptime needs two independent vantages before it calls a target down. With one runner network, enabling a monitor takes the installation's External check URL (change it in Settings), or add a second location or give that monitor its own external check URL in its settings.

- **Ping, port, DNS, UDP, API-assertion, visual comparison and dependency monitors** are unsupported by this importer. It maps HTTP(S), keyword and heartbeat monitors. Browser checks are outside the supported public feature set.
- **Authentication, custom request headers and POST bodies** are not imported, because they can hold secrets. The monitor is created with a local credential reference such as `uptimerobot-123456`, which you set up on your own runner before enabling it.
- **Locations and regions.** UptimeRobot's own vantage points are not reproduced. Uptime checks from your runners.
- **Alert contacts and notification settings.** Reconnect destinations in Uptime under **Settings › Alerts**. Importing sends nothing to anyone.
- **Status pages** are a different product. Lamp is the public status page product.
- **Maintenance windows.** Set maintenance on the monitor in Uptime.
- **Tags and groups**, and certificate or domain expiry reminders.
- **Ignored certificate errors and turned-off redirects.** Uptime fails a check on a certificate error and follows redirects, validating each hop. The preview notes monitors where UptimeRobot did otherwise.

UptimeRobot's log export is a CSV of past events. Uptime recognises it and counts its rows in a preview, for example "120 rows, provenance: UptimeRobot log export, not stored as evidence". Nothing applies from it, and the preview is cancelled as soon as it is shown, so neither the file nor its plan is stored. No row becomes an Uptime check, incident or state, so old history can never confirm a failure, close an incident or change the 24-hour and 7-day figures. Your Uptime history starts with your first Uptime check.

The mapping follows the field names in UptimeRobot's published v3 API description. The synthetic-file journey covers preview, paused apply, reading the saved definitions, export and undo, including status sets/ranges and both keyword conditions. Live account extraction, alert-contact mapping and status-page handoff are not implemented by this importer. It has not been tested with an export from a real UptimeRobot account. UptimeRobot does not publish its log export columns; Uptime looks for a date or time column and an event column.

Business can drive this same saved-monitors mapping through Base's optional import door. It starts off. In **Settings › Integrations**, turn on **Allow owner-approved imports from Business** under **Business imports**; it saves as you change it. When Run Edit Run installs Uptime for a Business plan you approved, it sets `RER_IMPORT_DOOR=on` and the door opens with your first owner claim instead; switching it off there keeps it off, and a later claim or sign-in never turns it back on. A self-hosted `rer deploy` never sets the variable. The installation must already have its owner-claim issuer, installation ID, app origin and public signing-key ring configured. Open Locations first to establish its first location. No UptimeRobot credential is sent to Uptime.

The door accepts saved v3 pages as NDJSON (one `{data: [...], nextLink: ...}` page per line), up to 2 MiB and 500 source records; a source monitor's `id` keeps its identity across moves, and one without an `id` is identified by its position. Grants name the `uptimerobot` namespace; Uptime's server-side source list, the same one the move-in screen uses (`uptimerobot`, `pingdom`, `betterstack-heartbeats`, `uptimerobot-log` and one `uptime.monitors:<id>` namespace per reviewed definition file), refuses any other namespace with 403 `unknown_import_source` before writing anything. Saved pages must not carry live credentials: an upload holding one by the import door's own rule in a request field Uptime withholds (a credential-named field such as `httpPassword` or `apiKey`, a credential header such as `Authorization` under `customHttpHeaders`, or a URL with a user name and password) is refused with 400 `source_secrets_withheld` and discarded. Run Edit Run's UptimeRobot export removes exactly these before upload and marks each one (`"[removed]"`, a `removed@` user name, `?api_key=removed`), so its pages are accepted as they are, user names, other headers and request bodies included. Uptime withholds every request field itself: `httpUsername`, `httpPassword`, `customHttpHeaders` and `postValueData` values, Pingdom header values, user names, passwords and post data never reach a monitor, revision, plan or import record, and the entry is mapped to a local credential reference or refused exactly as the move-in screen does (a monitor whose URL carries a user name or a credential parameter such as `?api_key=` is refused alone, with its reason, and the door removes the parameter's value). The door keeps an upload's original bytes under their hash, installation-local, as Base's door does, except that a plan drops them when they held a URL credential part, even a marker. It uses the existing importer’s supported types, differences, credential references and validation. A record matches the monitor its earlier move created, otherwise the monitor with its name, which it changes in place and leaves running or paused as it was. Imported monitors count toward the installation’s ordinary monitor limit and arrive paused. Catch-ups retain source IDs; Base refuses native edit conflicts and reports missing source records without deleting them.

The signed-grant protocol is documented in [the vendored Base door](https://github.com/runeditrun/base/blob/052e5ea88c1e7b73cca10c4813524a5f72580af8/modules/import-kit/src/door/README.md) (rer 0.2.71). The same pipeline is the owner's own import path: **Settings › Backup and files** and `node scripts/definitions.mjs apply` call `POST /api/operator/import/{uploads,plan,apply,status,reconcile,undo}` with the owner's session, the exact app `Origin` and an `X-Import-Source` header naming the source, whether or not Business imports are on. There is no other import route. Each request needs a fresh short-lived ES256 grant. Upload checks every chunk and the complete bundle hash. Plan writes no native monitor or evidence; apply requires the retained plan’s exact reviewed fingerprint and signed owner approval. Reconcile reads the actual monitors and import provenance. Original bytes, plans and grants stay in this installation and are excluded from portable archives; native definitions and revisions use Uptime’s existing archive.

Business imports appear in **Settings › Backup and files** under **Past imports** with “Approved via Business by” the owner, the approval time and fingerprint; the owner's own door imports read “Approved by”. An apply that fails shows as **Apply failed** with its reason code, never as applied: that plan cannot be applied again, so plan the export again for a fresh approval. If the failed apply had already written some monitors, **Undo this batch** rolls it back first. **Undo this batch** remains available even after Business is switched off or its signing key is revoked. Undo releases the monitors a move created: they stay in Uptime, paused, with their revisions and evidence. Undo leaves a monitor the owner edited or enabled since the move as the owner left it and reports it in the batch; it releases the rest, and the batch reads as undone with its time. Undo snapshots newest first. Each source keeps one lineage, so a later move of the same source is a catch-up of the last applied snapshot, or a new baseline once every snapshot is undone. A new baseline never takes back a released monitor: its plan explains each such record ("Imported before and released by undo or erasure; it stays in Uptime as its own monitor. Erase that monitor to import it again.") instead of offering it as an addition, and an unchanged released record reads as unchanged. Reconcile and catch-up planning read the imported set in a number of queries that does not grow with the set or the chain: in a chain of 15 catch-ups at the 100-monitor limit, every catch-up from the second on plans with the same statement count (the first reads no earlier catch-up's history, so it needs three fewer), and every reconcile after the base import reads the same count.

Erasing a monitor also withdraws the indivisible source exports of its source's lineage and retires that lineage's retained uploads, plans, approvals, failure facts and undo authority, in the same database transaction. An archive Business took of an export that names the monitor goes the same way, even when it is the only copy left: its bytes are withdrawn, its header (id, tool, time, hash, size and counts) stays, and `restore-check` answers 410 `archive_withdrawn`. The next move of that source starts a new baseline, in which the erased monitor's record can be imported again. Other monitors from that export remain in Uptime with their own revisions and evidence; they are released, so that baseline explains them instead of re-creating them.

During a switch-over, Run Edit Run checks what Uptime sent and created by calling `POST /api/rer/cutover-status` with a signed `cutover-status` grant and the body `{"since": "<ISO time>"}`. It is read-only and answers counts, ids and hosts only: `deliveries`, one `{destination_id, host, sent_since, ok_since}` per alert destination (a webhook or Slack destination's host, `null` for email; deliveries that made an attempt since that time and those the receiver accepted), and `created_since: {monitors, incidents}`. Destination names, email addresses, endpoint paths, signing secrets and monitor or incident content never leave Uptime. A self-hosted install without the owner-claim trust answers 404; an unsigned request 401; any other grant, an expired one, one for another installation, owner or key, and a revoked key 403; a request other than POST 405; and a body without an ISO `since` 400.

To revoke access, switch Business imports off or expand **Grant signing keys**, select the key ID and save. Revoking a key is permanent for that ID, including after re-enabling imports; configure a new signing-key ID to grant access again. A synthetic public-door journey covers off-by-default 404, upload, zero-write native plan, fingerprint-checked apply, reconciliation, history, undo and persistent revocation, and runs Base's public conformance check through both the Business and owner doors. No real customer export was used.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $UPTIMEROBOT_READ_ONLY_KEY" "https://api.uptimerobot.com/v3/monitors?limit=200" > uptimerobot-monitors.json
```

The response is one page, `{"data": [...], "nextLink": ...}`. If `nextLink` is not null, fetch that link too and append the next page to the same file. Uptime reads pages written one after another, or a JSON array of pages. Keep the file private: it can contain your heartbeat URLs and request settings.

A monitor CSV headed `Friendly Name,URL/IP,Type,Interval (min)` is not the saved v3 format this importer reads. Use the JSON response above, including every page. ## Keep monitors as a reviewed file, or move from UptimeRobot

Open **Settings › Backup and files** in the console to preview an `uptime.monitors.json` definition file, or saved UptimeRobot v3 `GET /monitors` pages, before anything changes. The preview lists each entry as create, unchanged, change, refused or unsupported, with every difference from the source spelled out, and ends with a plan digest. Every import runs through the owner's import door, the same pipeline Business uses, and apply writes exactly that reviewed plan: new monitors arrive paused, changes become new revisions that keep each monitor's on/off and maintenance state, and nothing enables a monitor, issues a heartbeat token, sends a notification or touches a destination. Each apply is a batch you can undo; undo leaves a monitor edited or enabled since alone and says so, and never removes history. Request headers, bodies and passwords in a file are withheld before it uploads and are never stored. **Export monitors** writes the same file back. With dev stopped, `node scripts/definitions.mjs preview|apply|export|batches|undo` runs the same engine locally. An UptimeRobot log export is only counted as history. See [Definition files](docs/definitions.md) and [Moving from UptimeRobot](docs/moving-from-uptimerobot.md); no real UptimeRobot export has been tested.
